definition_zh: 倒影；映像；反射；反映；深思；反思；想法；责备
definition_en: an image sent back from a surface, the throwing back of light or sound, a sign of something, or careful thought about the past

scene: 清晨起雾，玻璃窗上蒙着一层薄雾气，屋里的人影若隐若现。 She saw her own reflection in the misted window.
sceneCN: 这里 reflection 是「映像；倒影」（第 1 个义项：表面送回的形象）；句意：她在蒙着雾气的窗上看见自己的映像。场景要点：薄雾、玻璃、模糊的人影。

senses.title: The image sent back by a surface
senses.definition: an image of someone or something that appears in a mirror, water, or glass
senses.definitionCN: 出现在镜子、水面或玻璃中的人或物的形象
senses.example: The moon doubled itself in the still reflection of the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 月亮在海湾平静的倒影里又多了一个自己。
senses.why: The bent-back ray carries the picture to the eye: the image is what returns.
senses.whyCN: 折返的光线把图画带给眼睛：映像就是「回来的那幅画」。

senses.title: The throwing back of light or sound
senses.definition: the physical process of light, heat, or sound striking a surface and being sent back
senses.definitionCN: 光、热或声到达表面后被送回的物理过程
senses.example: The glow of sunset was a reflection off the wet pavement.
senses.exampleCN: 那片夕阳的亮光是湿漉漉的人行道反射出来的。
senses.why: Here the noun names the bending itself, not the picture: the event of the ray returning.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词命名的是「折返」这件事本身，而不是那幅画：即光线返回的过程。

senses.title: A clear sign of something
senses.definition: a thing that shows the true nature or state of something else, as in a reflection of
senses.definitionCN: 显示另一事物真实性质或状态的迹象，用于 a reflection of 结构
senses.example: Her patience with students is a reflection of her own schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 她对学生的耐心是她自己受教育经历的写照。
senses.why: A surface cannot invent what it sends back: so any faithful sign is called a reflection of what made it.
senses.whyCN: 表面无法凭空造出送回的东西：所以任何忠实的迹象都被称为「其来源的反映」。

senses.title: Careful thought
senses.definition: quiet, serious thinking about something, especially over some time
senses.definitionCN: 对某事安静而郑重的思索，常历时较久
senses.example: After a week of reflection he withdrew the application.
senses.exampleCN: 沉思一周后，他撤回了申请。
senses.why: The mind turns the beam inward and the picture returns to itself: thought is light bent back in the head.
senses.whyCN: 心灵把光束转向内部，图画回到自身：思考就是脑中折回的光。

senses.title: A thought written down
senses.definition: an idea or opinion produced by thinking, often shared in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 思考产生的想法或见解，常通过言谈或文字表达
senses.example: The last page of her diary holds her reflections on the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 她日记的最后一页写满了这次旅程的感想。
senses.why: What the bent-back beam showed becomes a shareable picture: an inward image put into words.
senses.whyCN: 折回光束所照见的，变成可以分享的图画：内在的映像落成了文字。

senses.title: Credit or blame carried back to someone
senses.definition: an effect on the good or bad opinion of someone, as in cast a reflection on
senses.definitionCN: 对某人名誉好坏的影响，用于 cast a reflection on 结构
senses.example: The bribery scandal cast a reflection on the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 受贿丑闻给整个部门带来了不良影响。
senses.why: Deeds, like light, bend back onto the surface behind them: the group shares the image the act returns.
senses.whyCN: 行为如光，会折回其身后的表面：集体分担行为折回的那幅影像。

intro.en: Reflection comes from Latin reflexionem, the noun of action from reflectere 'to bend back'. The classical Latin form had an -x- (reflexio); the -ct- spelling was restored in learned English usage, and both spellings coexisted for centuries.
intro.cn: reflection 来自拉丁语 reflexionem，即 reflectere「弯回」的行为名词。古典拉丁语形式带 -x-（reflexio）；-ct- 拼写在英语书面语中被恢复，两种拼写曾并存数个世纪。

items.en: Reflexio / reflectionem is built on reflectere: re- 'back' + flectere 'bend'. It named the act of bending back, used of rays and of thought alike.
items.cn: reflexio／reflectionem 建立在 reflectere 上：re-「回」+ flectere「弯曲」。它命名「弯回」这一行为，既用于光线，也用于思想。

items.en: The noun appears in English by the late fourteenth century in learned contexts, chiefly of the turning back of rays, sight, and attention.
items.cn: 名词到十四世纪晚期已见于英语的学术语境，主要指光线、视线与注意力的折返。

items.en: The spellings reflexion and reflection coexisted in English for centuries; reflection gradually prevailed in British usage and became universal in American usage.
items.cn: reflexion 与 reflection 两种拼写在英语中并存数百年；reflection 渐成英式主流，并在美式英语中成为唯一形式。

items.en: The mental senses 'serious thought' and 'an idea resulting from thought' develop in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, extending the optical metaphor.
items.cn: 「郑重思考」与「思考所得的见解」等心智义在十六、十七世纪发展起来，延伸了光学的比喻。

items.en: Today the noun covers the mirrored image, the physical process, the faithful sign, the act of thought, its written result, and the honour or shame carried back to a person.
items.cn: 如今这个名词涵盖：镜像、物理过程、忠实的迹象、思考行为、其文字成果，以及折回某人身上的荣辱。

note.en: The first group gathers the flectere 'bend' family around the noun. The second group compares the nouns that name images, signs, and thought.
note.cn: 第一组汇集围绕该名词的 flectere「弯曲」词族。第二组比较命名影像、迹象与思考的名词。

entries.definition: an older British spelling of reflection, still seen in formal writing. Same word, older clothes.
entries.definitionCN: reflection 的旧式英拼，仍偶见于正式书面语。同一个词，旧式写法。

entries.definition: describing surfaces that send light back, or people given to thought. It is the adjective of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能反光的表面，或惯于思考的人。它是词族中的形容词。

entries.definition: an automatic bodily response, from the same Latin participle. It keeps the classical -x- spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的自动反应，出自同一拉丁分词，保留了古典的 -x- 拼写。

entries.definition: the bending of something aside from its course. Same noun shape, different direction.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物偏离路线的弯折。名词形式相同，方向不同。

entries.definition: a change in the tone of the voice or the form of a word. It bends inward, not back.
entries.definitionCN: 语调或词形的变化。它向内曲折，而非折回。

entries.definition: a picture of something, made by light, art, or imagination. Image is the picture itself; reflection adds the idea of return.
entries.definitionCN: 由光、艺术或想象造出的图像。image 只是图画；reflection 多一层「折返」之意。

entries.definition: a sound sent back, or an idea repeated. For sound, echo does the work that reflection does for light.
entries.definitionCN: 被送回的声音，或被重复的观点。声音领域的 echo 相当于光领域的 reflection。

entries.definition: long, deep thinking, often with a spiritual tinge. It stresses the act; reflection can also name the result.
entries.definitionCN: 长久而深入的思考，常带灵性色彩。它强调过程；reflection 还可指思考的结果。

entries.definition: steady, attentive thinking or gazing. It is longer and quieter than ordinary reflection.
entries.definitionCN: 专注的凝视或思索。比一般的 reflection 更久、更静。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'back' + flectere 'bend', the noun suffix -ion, the family reflex, reflective and inflection, and the two spellings reflexion and reflection.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-「回」加 flectere「弯曲」，名词后缀 -ion，词族 reflex、reflective、inflection，以及 reflexion／reflection 两种拼写。

normal.en: The noun keeps the verb's grammar: reflection is the thing or the act of reflecting.
normal.cn: 名词继承动词的语法：reflection 就是 reflect 的结果或行为。

normal.en: The suffix -ion turns an action into a noun, like action from act.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ion 把动作变成名词，正如 act 变成 action。

normal.en: Reflex is the classical -x- cousin: the knee bends back all by itself.
normal.cn: reflex 是古典 -x- 拼写的表亲：膝盖自己就「折」了回去。

normal.en: Mirror, water and glass all give reflections; reports and faces give reflections of deeper things.
normal.cn: 镜子、水、玻璃给出倒影；报告与表情则给出深层事物的反映。

normal.en: After some reflection means after the beam has been bent inward and returned.
normal.cn: after some reflection 就是光束向内折返并返回之后。

abstract.en: Stand at the edge of a still lake at dusk: your double looks back up at you from the water.
abstract.cn: 黄昏时站在静湖边：你的「分身」从水里仰头望着你。

abstract.en: A quiet room with one lamp is enough for reflection: the mind leans over its own picture.
abstract.cn: 一间亮着一盏灯的静室就够人反思了：心灵俯身端详自己的图画。

abstract.en: Reflection is the answer a surface gives back: it never speaks first.
abstract.cn: reflection 是表面给出的回答：它从不先开口。

examples.en: The reflection of the towers stretched all the way across the river.
examples.cn: 高楼的倒影一直铺到河对岸。

examples.en: His bad temper is a reflection of the pressure he is under.
examples.cn: 他的坏脾气是他所承受压力的反映。

examples.en: She read her old essays and smiled at the reflections of her younger self.
examples.cn: 她读旧日的文章，为年轻时写下的感想而微笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞福来克申」——瑞福把申请书贴在镜前来克申，镜里也有一份折回来 → reflection 倒影；反思（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 reflectere 的行为名词 reflexionem「弯回之事」（re- 回 + flectere 弯曲），核心是「被送回来的东西或折返的过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of reflection, all naming what comes back: an image, a ray, a true sign, a thought, a written idea, and the honour or shame a deed returns to its doer.
sensesIntro.cn: reflection 的六个义项都在命名「回来的东西」：一幅影像、一束光、一个真切的迹象、一番思考、一段写下的感想，以及行为折回本人的荣辱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the picture or process that comes back from a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：从表面折返回来的图画或过程。

chain: THE DEED RETURNS TO ITS DOER

branches.en: OPTICS: the image in the mirror and the bending of the ray itself are the two physical faces of one event.
branches.cn: 光学：镜中的影像与光线折返的过程，是同一件事的两个物理侧面。

branches.en: SIGN: anything that faithfully shows its origin is a reflection of that origin.
branches.cn: 迹象：凡忠实显示其来源之物，皆为其来源的反映。

branches.en: THOUGHT: the inward-bent beam produces the act of thinking and the ideas it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 思考：向内折回的光束产生思考行为，也留下思考的成果。

branches.en: REPUTATION: deeds bend back onto the person and group behind them.
branches.cn: 名誉：行为折回到其背后的人与集体身上。

branches.en: SURFACES EVERYWHERE: water, glass, facts and behaviour all share one job — returning what arrives.
branches.cn: 处处皆表面：水、玻璃、事实与行为共享同一份工作——把来到的东西送回去。

intro.en: Reflection adds the Latin noun suffix -ion to the stem flectere 'bend' with the prefix re- 'back'. The same stem with other prefixes gives inflection, deflection and circumflex.
intro.cn: reflection 在词干 flectere「弯曲」加前缀 re-「回」之上，附加拉丁名词后缀 -ion。同一词干配其他前缀生出 inflection、deflection、circumflex。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is reflexio, from reflectere 'bend back'. The action suffix -io / -ionem is among the most productive noun endings Latin handed to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 reflexio，出自 reflectere「弯回」。行为后缀 -io／-ionem 是拉丁语传给英语的最高产名词词尾之一。

items.meaning: the act or result of bending back
items.meaningCN: 倒影；反映；反思（re- 回 + flectere 弯曲 + -ion 行为名词）
items.example: Her essay is a reflection on growing up.
items.exampleCN: 她的文章是对成长的反思。

items.meaningCN: reflection 的旧式拼写（保留古典 -x-）
items.example: Older books print reflexion where modern ones print reflection.
items.exampleCN: 旧书印作 reflexion，现代书印作 reflection。

items.meaning: sending back light; given to thought
items.meaningCN: 反光的；沉思的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The wet road was strangely reflective at night.
items.exampleCN: 湿漉漉的路面夜里反光异样地亮。

items.meaningCN: 自我反省（self- 自身 + reflection）
items.exampleCN: 写日记有助于自我反省。

items.meaning: a bend in tone or word form
items.meaningCN: 语调变化；屈折变化（in- 向内 + -ion）
items.example: A rising inflection can turn a statement into a question.
items.exampleCN: 上扬的语调能把陈述句变成疑问句。

items.meaning: a bend away from the course
items.example: The goalkeeper's deflection saved the goal.

items.meaning: the accent mark that bends over a vowel
items.meaningCN: 扬抑符（circum- 环绕 + flectere 弯曲）

items.meaning: an automatic response of the body
items.meaningCN: 反射动作（分词 flexus 缩略）
items.example: Pulling the hand away is a reflex.

items.meaningCN: 柔韧的；灵活的（-ible 表示可被…的）
items.exampleCN: 灵活的计划经得起意外。

items.structure: native English cousin of the bending idea
items.meaning: to force something out of a straight line
items.meaningCN: 弄弯（英语本土的「弯曲」近义词，词源不同）
items.example: Bend the wire into a hook.

senses.title: To throw something
senses.definition: to throw something with force, especially so that it lands some distance away
senses.definitionCN: 用力把某物扔出去，尤指扔到较远处
senses.example: He cast the rope toward the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他把绳子抛向岸边。
senses.why: The Norse source simply meant to throw, and that physical act remains the core of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语源词本义就是扔，这个身体动作始终是后面所有义项的核心。

senses.title: To choose actors for roles
senses.definition: to select actors for the parts in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 为戏剧或电影中的角色挑选演员
senses.example: They cast her as the queen.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让她演女王。
senses.why: Choosing an actor is pictured as throwing a person into a role, as if into a mould.
senses.whyCN: 选演员被想象成把人投进一个角色里，就像投进模具。

senses.title: The group of actors
senses.definition: all the actors who perform in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 参与一部戏剧或电影演出的全体演员
senses.example: The whole cast came on stage for the applause.
senses.exampleCN: 全体演员上台接受掌声。
senses.why: Once people have been thrown into their parts, the collection of them takes the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 人一旦被投进各自的角色，这一群人就沿用了同一个名词。

senses.title: To send light or a look
senses.definition: to cause light, shadow or a glance to fall on something
senses.definitionCN: 使光、影或目光落到某物上
senses.example: The tall buildings cast long shadows.
senses.exampleCN: 高楼投下长长的影子。
senses.why: Light thrown from a source behaves like an object thrown forward, so the verb covers casting shadows.
senses.whyCN: 从光源甩出的光就像被抛出的物体，于是动词也覆盖了投下影子。

senses.title: To pour metal into a mould
senses.definition: to pour melted metal into a shaped container so that it hardens into an object
senses.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属倒入模具，冷却后成为物件
senses.example: The workers cast the bell in one piece.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们一次浇铸成了这口钟。
senses.why: Molten metal is literally thrown into a mould, keeping the old sense of a forceful pour.
senses.whyCN: 熔化的金属确实是被「倒抛」进模具，保留了用力倾倒的旧义。

intro.en: Cast came from Old Norse rather than Latin, and one physical sense of throwing spread into acting, light and metalwork.
intro.cn: cast 来自古诺斯语而非拉丁语，一个扔的动作向外扩展到表演、光线和金属加工。

items.en: A reconstructed verb for throwing or tossing underlies the Norse word.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示投掷的原始日耳曼语动词，是诺斯语词的来源。

items.en: Kasta meant to throw, and Norse settlers brought it into northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kasta 意为投掷，随北欧移民进入英格兰北部。

items.en: Casten spreads from throwing objects to throwing light, looks and dice.
items.cn: 中古英语 casten 从扔物体扩展到投光、投目光和掷骰子。

items.en: Metalwork gives the sense of pouring molten metal into a mould.
items.cn: 金属加工带来把熔融金属倒入模具的义项。

items.en: The theatre takes cast for the selection of actors and then for the whole company.
items.cn: 十七世纪戏剧界用 cast 指挑选演员，进而指整个演员班底。

items.en: Modern English keeps all these branches, from casting a vote to a plaster cast.
items.cn: 现代英语保留全部分支，从投票到石膏铸型。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the casting and throwing family, while the meaning group lists other throwing verbs.
note.cn: 形近组沿铸造与投掷词族展开，近义组列出其他表示扔的动词。

entries.definition: the act of shaping metal or choosing actors
entries.definitionCN: 铸造或选角的行为

entries.definition: a person who casts metal, or a small wheel
entries.definitionCN: 铸工，或家具下的小轮

entries.definition: a person left alone after a shipwreck
entries.definitionCN: 海难后被弃在荒处的人

entries.definition: to send something through the air with the hand
entries.definitionCN: 用手把东西抛向空中

entries.definition: to throw something with great force
entries.definitionCN: 用力猛掷

entries.definition: to throw something quickly and carelessly
entries.definitionCN: 快速随意地扔

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the single image of throwing and show how each phrase extends it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子守住「扔」这一个画面，并展示每个搭配如何延伸它。

normal.en: Every sense begins with a hand throwing: a rope, a vote, a shadow, a role or molten metal.
normal.cn: 每个义项都从一只手扔出去开始：绳子、选票、影子、角色或熔融金属。

normal.en: Cast a vote pictures the ballot as a small object thrown into a box.
normal.cn: cast a vote 把选票想象成被扔进箱子的小物件。

normal.en: Cast a shadow keeps the image literal: light throws a dark shape onto the ground.
normal.cn: cast a shadow 保留字面画面：光把一块暗形扔到地面上。

normal.en: The past tense is cast, not casted, so the verb looks unchanged.
normal.cn: 过去式是 cast 而不是 casted，所以动词看起来没有变化。

normal.en: Casting covers both metal and actors because both involve pouring something into a prepared shape.
normal.cn: casting 同时指铸金属和选演员，因为两者都是把东西倒进预备好的形状里。

abstract.en: Picture a fisherman flinging a net in a wide arc.
abstract.cn: 想象渔夫把网甩出一个大弧。

abstract.en: Picture a director pointing at one actor in a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象导演在挤满人的房间里指向一位演员。

abstract.en: Picture sparks flying as hot metal fills a clay mould.
abstract.cn: 想象炽热的金属注入泥模时火星四溅。

examples.en: She cast the line far into the river.
examples.cn: 她把钓线远远抛进河里。

examples.en: The film has a strong cast.
examples.cn: 这部电影的演员阵容很强。

examples.en: The tree cast a cool shadow over the bench.
examples.cn: 那棵树在长椅上投下一片凉影。

dict_mnemonic.text: cast 的核心动作就是「扔」：把绳子扔出去，把票扔进箱，把演员扔进角色，把铁水扔进模具。

root: 源自古诺斯语 kasta（投掷），属日耳曼语词，无拉丁语祖先；由「扔」这一动作扩展出投射、选角与铸造诸义。

sensesIntro.en: One throwing gesture gives the rope, the vote, the shadow, the actor and the molten metal.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个投掷动作先后给出绳子、选票、影子、演员和熔融金属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sending something forward through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西向前甩到空中。

branches.en: The literal throw stays in fishing, dice and ropes.
branches.cn: 字面的扔保留在钓鱼、掷骰和抛绳中。

branches.en: Light thrown from a source lays a shadow down.
branches.cn: 从光源甩出的光把影子放倒在地上。

branches.en: Actors are thrown into parts, and the group of them becomes the cast.
branches.cn: 演员被投进角色，这一群人就成为演员阵容。

branches.en: Molten metal is poured into a mould and hardens into a cast object.
branches.cn: 熔融金属被倒入模具，凝固成铸件。

branches.en: Both keep the force of a deliberate, aimed pour or toss.
branches.cn: 两者都保留了有目标、有力度的倾倒或抛掷感。

intro.en: Cast builds compounds and agent nouns rather than taking classical affixes.
intro.cn: cast 主要构成复合词和表施动者的名词，不常接古典词缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，因此不列拉丁同源词。

definition_zh: 愤怒；怒气；义愤；使发怒；激怒
definition_en: a strong feeling of displeasure caused by something unfair, hurtful or frustrating; also to make someone feel this
core_image: 胸口一团越收越紧的热，最后从喉咙冲出来
scene: 修车铺里，车主发现刚换的零件又坏了，拳头慢慢握紧。 His anger rose when the mechanic admitted using a second-hand part.
sceneCN: 这里 anger 是「愤怒、怒气」（第 1 个义项：因不公或受挫而生的强烈不快）；句意为修理工承认用了二手零件时，他的怒气升了上来。画面里有修车铺、坏掉的零件与握紧的拳头。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「生气的；愤怒的」
由 angry 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愤怒地」
由 angry 加 looking 构成的复合形容词，义为「面带怒色的」

senses.title: The feeling of anger
senses.definition: a strong feeling of displeasure and hostility caused by an injury, injustice or frustration
senses.definitionCN: 因受到伤害、不公或挫折而产生的强烈不快与敌意
senses.example: She felt a sudden anger at the unfairness of the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 这项决定的不公让她忽然感到愤怒。
senses.why: Old Norse angr meant grief and distress; anger is that tight, painful pressure turned outward.
senses.whyCN: 古诺尔斯语 angr 意为「悲伤、痛苦」；anger 就是那股收紧的痛感转而向外冲。

senses.title: An outburst or episode
senses.definition: a particular occasion or burst of angry feeling
senses.definitionCN: 某一次爆发出来的愤怒情绪
senses.example: He left the room in anger and slammed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他愤怒地离开房间，把门摔上。
senses.why: A mass noun can be counted when it comes in waves, so one surge of the feeling is an anger.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的情绪一旦成波涌来就能计数，于是一股涌起的怒气也可以说成一次 anger。

senses.title: To make someone angry
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel anger
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生愤怒
senses.example: The delays angered the passengers waiting on the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 延误激怒了在站台上等候的乘客。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction: instead of feeling the pressure, someone applies it to another.
senses.whyCN: 动词把方向反过来：不是自己承受那股压力，而是把它施加到别人身上。

senses.title: Anger at injustice
senses.definition: anger felt on moral grounds, especially at injustice done to others
senses.definitionCN: 出于道德理由产生的愤怒，尤指因他人遭受不公而愤怒
senses.example: Their anger at the pollution grew into a campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对污染的愤怒后来发展成一场运动。
senses.why: The same pressure rises when a wrong is witnessed, and society gives it a respectable name.
senses.whyCN: 目睹不公时同一股压力也会升起，社会给它一个体面的名字，叫义愤。

senses.title: The wrath of a god
senses.definition: in older and literary writing, the destructive displeasure of a god or fate
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文学作品中，指神或命运带有毁灭性的不悦
senses.example: The old story tells of the anger of the gods at human pride.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老故事讲述众神对人类傲慢的愤怒。
senses.why: Human anger writ large becomes a cosmic force, which is why wrath belongs to gods in epic writing.
senses.whyCN: 把人的愤怒放大，就成了宇宙级的力量，因此在史诗里「愤怒」属于神。

intro.en: Anger came from Old Norse, and its oldest sense is closer to grief than to rage.
intro.cn: anger 来自古诺尔斯语，它最早的义项更接近「悲痛」而不是「暴怒」。

items.en: The noun angr meant 'grief, sorrow, distress'. The emotional starting point is pain rather than attack.
items.cn: 名词 angr 意为「悲伤、痛苦、苦恼」，情感的起点是痛，而不是攻击。

items.en: The related verb angra meant 'to grieve, to vex', already close to causing distress.
items.cn: 相关动词 angra 意为「使悲伤、使烦恼」，已经接近「使人痛苦」。

items.en: The root *angh- is generally reconstructed as 'tight, painfully constricted'. It also underlies Latin angere and angustus. The reconstruction is not a recorded word.
items.cn: 词根 *angh- 一般重构为「紧绷、痛苦地收缩」，拉丁语 angere 与 angustus 也出自这里。该重构不是有记录的词。

items.en: Latin angere meant 'to choke, strangle, torment', and angustus meant 'narrow'. Both preserve the image of tightness.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angere 意为「使窒息、扼住、折磨」，angustus 意为「狭窄」，两者都保留了「紧绷」的意象。

items.en: English borrowed the Norse noun as anger; the exact first date is uncertain because early spellings differ.
items.cn: 英语把诺尔斯语名词借入为 anger；由于早期拼写不同，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun and verb settle into the modern pair, and the adjective angry grows from the noun with -y.
items.cn: 名词与动词固定为现代的一对，形容词 angry 由名词加 -y 长出。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tightness root; the near-meaning group ranks degrees of displeasure from irritation to wrath.
note.cn: 形近组共享「紧绷」词根；近义组按不快程度排列，从轻微恼怒到盛怒。

entries.definition: Adjective: feeling or showing anger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「生气的、愤怒的」，由本词加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Extreme pain or distress of mind; from Latin angustia, narrowness, the same tightness image.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「极度痛苦、苦恼」，来自拉丁语 angustia「狭窄」，共享同一个「紧绷」意象。

entries.definition: Worried and tense; from Latin anxius, built on the same choking root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑的、紧张的」，来自拉丁语 anxius，词根同样表示「收紧、窒息」。

entries.definition: A German borrowing for deep anxiety or dread, from the same Germanic family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焦虑、恐惧」，借自德语，与本词同属日耳曼语族。

entries.definition: Violent, uncontrolled anger; louder and less reasoned than anger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「暴怒」，比 anger 更失控、更外显。

entries.definition: Extremely strong anger, often compared to a storm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「狂怒」，愤怒极强，常被比作风暴。

entries.definition: Mild annoyance, much weaker than anger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恼怒、不耐烦」，程度远轻于 anger。

entries.definition: Formal or literary anger, especially the anger of a powerful figure or god.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「盛怒、天罚之怒」，属正式或文学用词，尤指强者或神的愤怒。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Norse grief word, the tightness root, and the family of Latin cognates.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的诺尔斯语「悲伤」词、表示「紧绷」的词根，以及拉丁同源词族。

normal.en: AnGR meant grief first; anger is grief that has turned hot and outward.
normal.cn: angr 最初是「悲伤」；anger 是转为灼热并向外冲的悲伤。

normal.en: Angere is to choke in Latin, angustus is narrow: the root image is a tightened throat.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 angere 是「扼住」，angustus 是「狭窄」：词根意象是收紧的喉咙。

normal.en: Angry adds -y to the noun; angrily adds -ly to the adjective.
normal.cn: angry 在名词后加 -y，angrily 在形容词后加 -ly。

normal.en: In anger is a fixed phrase for acting while the feeling is still hot.
normal.cn: in anger 是固定短语，指在怒气未消时行动。

normal.en: Righteous anger keeps the moral sense: the pressure rises at a wrong done to others.
normal.cn: righteous anger 保留道德义：这股压力因他人遭受不公而升起。

abstract.en: Picture a fist slowly closing around a small stone until the knuckles go white.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头慢慢握住一颗小石头，直到指节变白。

abstract.en: Picture steam building under a lid that shakes but has not yet lifted.
abstract.cn: 想象蒸气在锅盖下积聚，盖子震动却还没有被顶开。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow corridor that becomes narrower with every step, the walls pressing inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条越走越窄的走廊，两侧墙壁不断向内压来。

examples.en: His anger rose when the mechanic admitted using a second-hand part.
examples.cn: 修理工承认用了二手零件时，他的怒气升了上来。

examples.en: She felt a sudden anger at the unfairness of the decision.
examples.cn: 这项决定的不公让她忽然感到愤怒。

examples.en: The delays angered the passengers waiting on the platform.
examples.cn: 延误激怒了在站台上等候的乘客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂哥」——昂着头、脖子绷紧，一口气堵在胸口：愤怒、怒气

root: 古诺尔斯语名词 angr「悲伤、苦恼」与动词 angra「使苦恼」是直接来源，可追溯到一般重构为 *angh-「紧绷、痛苦地收缩」的印欧词根；拉丁语 angere「扼住、折磨」与 angustus「狭窄」同出此根。词义从「痛苦」转为向外爆发的「愤怒」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow one pressure: the feeling itself, one burst of it, the act of causing it, the moral version felt at injustice, and the literary version magnified into divine wrath.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项沿着同一股压力展开：情绪本身、一次爆发、施加于人的动作、面对不公时的道德版本，以及被放大成神怒的文学版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heat and pressure build behind the ribs until they force their way out through the voice.
core.cn: 核心意象：热与压力在肋骨后面积聚，最后从声音里冲出来。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: the steady state of displeasure and hostility.
branches.cn: 情绪线：持续存在的不快与敌意状态。

branches.en: THE EPISODE LINE: the feeling counted as one surge or occasion.
branches.cn: 发作线：把情绪数成一次涌起或一个场合。

branches.en: THE CAUSING LINE: the verb turns the pressure outward onto someone else.
branches.cn: 施加线：动词把压力转向外，施加到别人身上。

branches.en: THE JUSTICE LINE: the same pressure rises when a wrong is witnessed.
branches.cn: 正义线：目睹不公时，同一股压力也会升起。

branches.en: THE EPIC LINE: human anger magnified until it belongs to gods.
branches.cn: 史诗线：把人的愤怒放大，直到它属于神。

intro.en: Anger is a Norse noun with a Germanic root; English adds the ordinary adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: anger 是一个带日耳曼词根的诺尔斯语名词，英语再为它加上普通的形容词与副词词尾。

scene: 社区中心的桌上摆着一叠申请表，志愿者在旁边教老人逐栏填写。 She applied for financial assistance after the storm.

senses.title: Help given to someone
senses.definition: help or support given to someone who needs it, especially in doing a task
senses.definitionCN: 给予需要之人的帮助或支持，尤指在做事时
senses.example: She applied for financial assistance after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后她申请了经济援助。
senses.why: The suffix -ance names the state or act of standing beside, so assistance is help seen as a thing given.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ance 命名「站在旁边」的状态或行为，所以 assistance 是被当作一件东西给出去的帮助。

senses.title: Financial or official aid
senses.definition: money or practical support provided by a government, charity, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 由政府、慈善机构或组织提供的钱款或实际支持
senses.example: The family received assistance with rent and heating.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人得到了房租与取暖方面的补助。
senses.why: Money is one form of standing beside someone, so the word widens from hands to funds.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是「站到某人身边」的一种形式，于是这个词从双手扩展到资金。

senses.title: The act of helping
senses.definition: the act of helping, often named in the phrase with the assistance of
senses.definitionCN: 帮助的行为，常用于短语 with the assistance of

senses.exampleCN: 在两名路人的帮助下，司机脱了身。
senses.why: Here the noun names the act rather than the thing, the standing-beside itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里的名词指动作而非物品，即「站在旁边」这件事本身。

intro.en: Assistance is the noun of assist, built with the French suffix -ance on the Latin verb for standing beside.
intro.cn: assistance 是 assist 的名词，用法语后缀 -ance 加在那个意为「站在旁边」的拉丁动词上。

items.en: The root 「*sta-」 meant 'to stand', the source of Latin sistere and of many standing words.
items.cn: 词根「*sta-」意为「站立」，是拉丁语 sistere 及许多表示站立的词的来源。

items.en: Assistere meant 'to stand beside', from ad- 'to' plus sistere 'to stand'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sistere「站立」构成。

items.en: The noun assistentia named the act of standing by to help.
items.cn: 名词 assistentia 指站在一旁给予帮助的行为。

items.en: French -ance shaped the noun as assistance, and English took it in that form.
items.cn: 法语后缀 -ance 把这个名词塑造成 assistance，英语直接以这一形式借入。

items.en: Assistance first meant the act of helping, then widened to the help itself, including money.
items.cn: assistance 最初指帮助的行为，后来扩展到帮助本身，包括钱款。

items.en: Modern use ranges from a hand at a door to state welfare and technical aid.
items.cn: 现代用法从门口伸出的一只手，一直延伸到国家福利与技术援助。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns close to assistance in form; the near-meaning group gathers help, aid, support and relief.
note.cn: 形近组收形式上与 assistance 接近的名词；近义组收帮助、援助、支持与救济。

entries.definition: Support or relief given to those in need.

normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从表格旁伸出的一只手，走到房租补助、一声喊出的提醒与国家救济。

abstract.en: Assistance is help seen from the side of the giver.
abstract.cn: assistance 是从给予者一侧看到的帮助。

abstract.en: Standing beside is the core of all three senses.
abstract.cn: 「站在旁边」是三个义项共同的核心。

examples.cn: 风暴过后她申请了经济援助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿西斯滕斯」——阿西斯滕斯站在表格旁，把手伸向填表的人：帮助

root: assistance 是 assist 的名词，后缀 -ance 来自法语，可追到拉丁语 assistentia。assist 又来自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sistere「站立」构成，词根意为「站」。因此 assistance 的核心就是「站在旁边」：既指给予他人的实际帮助，也指政府或组织提供的钱款与援助，还可以指帮助这一行为本身（常见于 with the assistance of）。它与 assess 的「坐在旁边称量」词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one standing-beside: help given in kind, money or official aid, and the act of helping itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共享同一个「站在旁边」：实物与人力上的帮助、金钱或官方援助，以及帮助这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand offered beside an application form with a grant figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：申请表旁伸出的一只手，表上写着补助金额。

branches.en: THE HAND LINE: practical help given to a person in need.
branches.cn: 援手线：给予需要之人的实际帮助。

branches.en: THE FUND LINE: money and official aid are another hand.
branches.cn: 资金线：钱款与官方援助是另一只手。

branches.en: THE ACT LINE: the noun also names helping itself.
branches.cn: 行动线：这个名词也指帮助这件事本身。

branches.en: THE WELFARE LINE: a volunteer's hand and a state grant share one purpose.
branches.cn: 福利线：志愿者的手与国家补助共享同一个目的。

branches.en: THE SERVICE LINE: help given and help performed are one event seen twice.
branches.cn: 服务线：给出的帮助与施予的行动，是同一件事的两种看法。

intro.en: Assistance is assist plus -ance; its family adds -ant and -ive, all built on standing beside.
intro.cn: assistance 是 assist 加 -ance，词族再加 -ant 与 -ive，全部建立在「站在旁边」上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin standing root sistere also produced resistance and insist, both keeping a firm stance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示站立的词根 sistere 还生出 resistance 与 insist，两者都保留「站稳立场」的意思。

items.en: It was used of rich colours and fine clothes.

items.en: It spread to landscapes and beautiful people.

intro.cn: convention 来自拉丁语 convenire（走到一起），由 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成。

items.cn: venire 意为来或到达。

items.en: Convenire meant to meet and to agree with one another.
items.cn: convenire 意为会面，也指彼此取得一致。

items.en: Conventio named a coming together and the agreement made.
items.cn: conventio 指聚到一起以及由此达成的约定。

items.en: French convention kept both the meeting and the custom senses.
items.cn: 法语 convention 同时保留聚会与习俗两层意思。

items.en: English convention meant an agreed custom.

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a habit a crowd repeats, then move to rules written by many parties and a hall full of strangers.

normal.en: A hall of name cards is the meeting sense made visible.

normal.en: Come together, agree, and repeat.

senses.whyCN: 空间上的拉伸变成时间或规模上的延长。

senses.title: Stretch out a hand
senses.definition: to stretch out a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 伸出身体的某一部分
senses.example: He extended his hand in greeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他伸出手来表示问候。
senses.why: The body repeats the outward stretch.
senses.whyCN: 身体重复了向外伸展的动作。

senses.title: Offer to someone
senses.definition: to offer help, thanks, or an invitation
senses.definitionCN: 给予帮助、感谢或邀请
senses.example: The school extended a warm welcome to us.
senses.exampleCN: 学校向我们表示了热烈欢迎。
senses.why: Reaching outward becomes offering something.
senses.whyCN: 向外伸手变成给出某物。

intro.en: Extend comes from Latin extendere, to stretch out, from ex- out and tendere to stretch.
intro.cn: extend 来自拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸），由 ex-（向外）与 tendere（拉）构成。

items.en: Ex- means out.
items.cn: ex- 意为向外。

items.en: Tendere means to stretch.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸。

items.en: Extendere means to stretch out.
items.cn: extendere 意为向外拉伸。

items.en: Extendre keeps the outward stretch.
items.cn: 古法语 extendre 保留向外伸展之义。

items.en: Extend covers space, time, and offers.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extend 涵盖空间、时间与给予。

note.en: Extend means stretch out; intend means plan.
note.cn: extend 是伸展开，intend 则是打算。

entries.definition: to plan to do something
entries.definitionCN: 打算

entries.definition: to go to an event or place
entries.definitionCN: 出席

entries.definition: to compete or argue

entries.definition: to make longer or wider
entries.definitionCN: 拉伸

entries.definition: to make something longer
entries.definitionCN: 延长

entries.definition: to become larger

normalIntro.en: Extend is the act of stretching something outward in space, time, or gesture.
normalIntro.cn: extend 是把事物在空间、时间或动作上向外伸展。

normal.en: The garden extends down to the lake.
normal.cn: 花园一直延伸到湖边。

normal.en: They extended the deadline by two days.
normal.cn: 他们把截止日期延长了两天。

normal.en: She extended her hand to help him up.
normal.cn: 她伸手把他扶起来。

normal.en: The company extended an offer to her.
normal.cn: 公司向她发出了聘用邀请。

normal.en: The shelf extends along the whole wall.
normal.cn: 架子沿着整面墙延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a road running straight to the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路笔直伸向地平线。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand reaching across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸过桌面。

abstract.en: Think of a calendar with extra days added.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上又添了几天。

examples.en: The desert extends far beyond the town.
examples.cn: 沙漠远远延伸到城镇之外。

examples.en: We extended the visit for another week.
examples.cn: 我们把访问又延长了一周。

examples.en: He extended his hand to the visitor.
examples.cn: 他向访客伸出了手。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（向外）加 tend（拉伸）：向外拉长，就是 extend（延伸、延长）。

root: 源自拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸），由 ex-（向外）与 tendere（拉）构成，核心义「向外伸展」。

sensesIntro.en: Extend means to reach across space, make longer or larger, stretch out a hand, or offer something.
sensesIntro.cn: extend 意为在空间中延伸、使更长更大、伸出手，或给予某物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road stretching to the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸向地平线的一条路。

branches.en: The base sense is stretching across space.
branches.cn: 基础义是在空间中伸展。

branches.en: Stretching becomes longer time or larger size.
branches.cn: 伸展变成时间更长或规模更大。

branches.en: The body repeats the outward stretch.
branches.cn: 身体重复向外伸展的动作。

branches.en: Reaching out becomes giving or offering.
branches.cn: 向外伸出变成给予或提供。

branches.en: Spatial reach and temporal extension share one motion.
branches.cn: 空间延伸与时间延长共享同一动作。

intro.en: Extend belongs to the Latin tendere family, like extend, intend, and attend.
intro.cn: extend 属于拉丁语 tendere 词族，与 intend、attend 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin extendere, tendere, and the prefix ex- are the source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extendere、tendere 与前缀 ex- 是来源要素。

items.example: The line extends to the door.
The offer extends to all students.
items.exampleCN: 这项优惠面向所有学生。
这座房子有宽阔的花园。

items.meaning: the size or degree of something
items.example: The extent of the damage is unclear.

items.meaning: the state of being stretched tight
a habit of moving or acting in one way

definition_zh: 节目；节目单；计划；方案；（计算机）程序；规划；用程序控制
definition_en: a show or broadcast, a plan of events, a set of instructions for a computer, or the act of arranging such things
core_image: 一页预先写好的清单，把要演出的曲目和要做的事按顺序排在上面
scene: 演出开始前，音乐厅门口的桌上放着一叠薄薄的小册子，观众一边排队一边翻看今晚的曲目。 The orchestra printed a slim programme listing every piece for the evening.
sceneCN: 这里取「节目单、节目」的意思（第 1 个义项：广播或演出的节目及其说明）；句意为乐团印了一本薄薄的节目单，列出当晚的每一首曲子。门口那叠小册子就是线索。

pos.zh: 节目；节目单；计划；方案；（计算机）程序

derivatives.zh: 由 programme 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「程序员」
由 programme 去 e 加 -ing 构成，义为「编程；节目编排」
由希腊词干 programmat- 加 -ic 构成，义为「纲领性的；按计划行事的」

senses.title: A show on television or radio
senses.definition: a show broadcast on television or radio, or the printed list of items in a performance
senses.definitionCN: 在电视或广播中播出的节目，也指演出前印好的曲目或环节清单
senses.example: Her cookery programme is shown every Sunday evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她的烹饪节目每周日晚播出。
senses.why: Greek programma was a public written notice, so the word began as something written down and read out before it named what was performed.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 programma 本指公开写出的通告，所以这个词最初是「写下来给人看的东西」，后来才指被演出或被播出的内容。

senses.title: A plan of events or actions
senses.definition: an organized plan listing the events, steps or work that will be done
senses.definitionCN: 把要做的事件、步骤或工作有条理地列出来的计划
senses.example: The government launched a programme to repair rural roads.
senses.exampleCN: 政府启动了修缮乡村道路的计划。
senses.why: A written notice also fixes an order, so the same word came to mean the ordered list of things to be done.
senses.whyCN: 写出来的通告同时规定了顺序，于是同一个词又指「按顺序排好的待办事项」，也就是计划。

senses.title: A set of instructions for a computer
senses.definition: a series of coded instructions that makes a computer perform a task
senses.definitionCN: 让计算机完成某项任务的一串编码指令
senses.example: He wrote a short programme that sorts the names alphabetically.
senses.exampleCN: 他写了一个短程序，把姓名按字母顺序排序。
senses.why: A computer follows a written sequence step by step, exactly as a theatre follows a printed running order, so the plan sense was reused for machine instructions.
senses.whyCN: 计算机一步步照着写好的顺序执行，就像剧场照着印好的流程单演出，于是「计划」这层意思被挪去指机器指令。

senses.title: To plan or arrange something
senses.definition: to arrange or set out a plan for an event, a machine or a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 为某项活动、某台机器或某个行动方案做出安排
senses.example: The festival was programmed months in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日的活动提前几个月就安排好了。
senses.why: If a programme is a written order of events, then to programme is to put things into that order, and later to feed that order into a machine.
senses.whyCN: 既然 programme 是写好的事件顺序，那么动词就是「把事情排进这个顺序」，后来也指把顺序输入机器。

intro.en: Programme goes back through French to a Greek word for a public written notice, built from a prefix meaning before and a verb meaning to write.
intro.cn: programme 经法语上溯到一个希腊词，本指公开写出的通告，由表示「在前」的前缀和表示「写」的动词构成。

items.en: The Greek prefix pro- meant before or in front, and graphein meant to write, so the pair described writing something beforehand.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 pro- 表示「在前」，动词 graphein 表示「写」，两者合起来就是「事先写出」。

items.en: Programma named a public notice put up in advance, such as an official announcement or a posted list.
items.cn: programma 指提前张贴出来的公开通告，例如官方告示或贴出的名单。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma unchanged from Greek and kept the sense of a written public notice.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入 programma，仍指写出来的公开通告。

items.en: French programme narrowed the word towards the printed list of a performance and towards a plan of work.
items.cn: 法语 programme 把词义收窄到演出的印刷节目单，以及工作的计划。

items.en: English took the French form as programme, kept it in Britain, and American usage shortened it to program.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 programme，英式保留此拼写，美式则简化为 program。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and relatives built on the same Greek root for writing; the near-meaning group gathers words for shows and plans.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊「写」词根上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示节目与计划的词。

entries.definition: The shorter American spelling, used for shows, plans and computer code.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的美式拼写，同样表示节目、计划与计算机代码。

entries.definition: A person who writes instructions for a computer.
entries.definitionCN: 编写计算机指令的人；程序员。

entries.definition: The work of writing computer code, or of arranging a schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 编写计算机代码的工作，或安排日程的工作。

entries.definition: Planned and organized according to a fixed set of aims.
entries.definitionCN: 按照一套固定目标来计划与组织的；纲领性的。

entries.definition: A performance or broadcast intended to entertain an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为娱乐观众而演出或播出的内容。

entries.definition: A radio or television transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 广播或电视的播出。

entries.definition: A plan that lists times and events.
entries.definitionCN: 列出时间与事项的计划；日程表。

entries.definition: A large plan, often official, for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而制定的大型计划，常指官方方案。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a written notice, so its memories hang on writing, listing and ordering, and on the machine that now follows such a list.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一份写出来的通告，所以记忆可以挂在「写、列、排序」上，也挂在照着清单执行的机器上。

normal.en: Greek graphein means to write, and English keeps that root in programme, diagram and grammar.
normal.cn: 希腊语 graphein 意为「写」，英语在 programme、diagram、grammar 里都保留了这个词根。

normal.en: The prefix pro- means before, so a programme is literally something written before the event happens.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示「在前」，所以 programme 字面上就是「活动开始之前写好的东西」。

normal.en: A theatre programme lists items in order and a computer program lists steps in order; the same idea of a written order runs through both.
normal.cn: 剧场节目单按顺序列出节目，计算机程序按顺序列出步骤，两者贯穿的是同一个「写好的顺序」。

normal.en: British English keeps the final -me and the double m, while American English drops them to spell it program.
normal.cn: 英式保留词尾的 me 与双写的 m，美式则省去这些字母，写成 program。

normal.en: Programmer only adds -er to the noun: the person who writes the code.
normal.cn: programmer 只是在名词后加 -er，指写代码的人。

abstract.en: A word that began as a poster and ended as code shows how writing can turn into action.
abstract.cn: 一个从海报变成代码的词，说明写下来的东西可以变成真正的行动。

abstract.en: Every list is a small promise about the future, which is why a show and a plan share one name.
abstract.cn: 每份清单都是对未来的小小承诺，所以一场演出和一份计划共用一个名字。

abstract.en: The machine does not invent the order; it only obeys the order that someone wrote down.
abstract.cn: 机器不会自己发明顺序，它只服从别人写下来的顺序。

examples.en: Her cookery programme is shown every Sunday evening.
examples.cn: 她的烹饪节目每周日晚播出。

examples.en: The city has programmed the traffic lights to favour buses.
examples.cn: 这座城市把交通灯设置成优先放行公交。

examples.en: Our school runs a programme for students who need extra help.
examples.cn: 我们学校为需要额外帮助的学生开办了一个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若格拉姆」——听着像「铺个栏目」，把栏目一条条铺开，就是节目单和计划。

root: 希腊语 pro-（在前）+ graphein（写）构成 programma，本指预先写出的公告；经拉丁语 programma 与法语 programme 进入英语，美式拼写简化为 program。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written list set out in advance; from it grow the show that follows the list, the plan behind it, the machine that executes it, and the act of arranging it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是事先写好的一份清单；由它长出照着清单演出的节目、清单背后的计划、执行清单的机器，以及安排清单的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet pinned up before an event, listing what will happen and in what order.
core.cn: 核心意象：活动开始前贴出的一张纸，写着要发生什么、按什么顺序发生。

branches.en: a printed sheet folded inside a concert hall seat
branches.cn: 音乐厅座椅上折好的印刷节目单

branches.en: a notice board announcing next month's events
branches.cn: 公告板上预告下月活动的通知

branches.en: a minister signing a three-year building plan
branches.cn: 部长签署一份三年建设计划

branches.en: a screen waiting for a line of code to run
branches.cn: 屏幕上等待一行代码运行

branches.en: an engineer slotting steps into the right order
branches.cn: 工程师把各个步骤排进正确的顺序

intro.en: The word rests on a Greek prefix and a Greek verb of writing, then passes through Latin and French before English adds its own endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语前缀和表示「写」的动词支撑，经拉丁语与法语传入英语，再由英语加上自己的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin took programma straight from Greek and used it for a written notice; the same root produced gramma, a written mark or letter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 programma，指写出的通告；同一词根还产生 gramma，指写下的符号或字母。

definition_zh: 占据；占用；占领；居住在；担任；使忙碌
definition_en: to take and hold something — a place, a space, a period of time, a post, or a person's attention
core_image: 一只手压住并攥紧一件东西，占住不放
scene: 阁楼里堆满纸箱，只留下通往窗户的一条窄路。 Boxes occupy most of the attic and leave only a narrow path to the window.
sceneCN: 这里 occupy 是「占去空间」（第 2 个义项：占据空间）；句意：箱子占去阁楼的大部分空间，只留下一条通往窗户的窄道。图中可辨识物件：成堆的纸箱、阁楼的横梁、窄窄的走道、窗子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 占据；占用；占领；担任；使忙于

collocations.zh: 担任某职位；占据某位置

derivatives.zh: 职业；占领；占用
职业的；职业引起的
居住者；占用者；乘坐者
占据者；占领者；住户
心事重重的；专注的（pre-“预先”+ occupy）

senses.title: Seize and hold: take possession
senses.definition: to take possession of a place or thing and keep control of it
senses.definitionCN: 取得对某地或某物的占有，并保持控制
senses.example: The troops occupied the fort before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 部队在黎明前占领了要塞。
senses.why: Latin occupare was an emphatic form of ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp, seize'. The core picture is a hand closing over something and not letting go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occupare 是 ob“覆在……之上”加 capere“抓、夺”的强调形式。核心画面就是一只手合拢抓住东西，不再放开。

senses.title: Take up space: fill a surface
senses.titleCN: 占去空间：铺满一块地方
senses.definition: to fill or cover an area of space, so that little room is left
senses.definitionCN: 填满或覆盖一块空间，几乎不留余地
senses.example: The piano occupies one corner of the living room.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴占了客厅的一个角落。
senses.why: A thing that holds a place holds it in the same grip: the floor under it is no longer free. Possession becomes measurement of space.
senses.whyCN: 占住一个位置的东西用的是同一个“握”：它下面的地板不再空着。占有于是变成对空间的度量。

senses.title: Take up time: fill a period
senses.titleCN: 占去时间：填满一段时间
senses.definition: to use up a period of time, leaving it unavailable for anything else
senses.definitionCN: 用掉一段时间，使其无法再做别的事
senses.example: The hearing occupied the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 听证会占了整整一个下午。
senses.why: Hours can be held just as floors can: once a period is gripped by an activity, it cannot be handed to another.
senses.whyCN: 小时和地板一样可以被“握住”：一段时间一旦被某项活动抓住，就无法再交给别的活动。

senses.title: Live in: hold as a home
senses.definition: to live in or use a building as one's home or base
senses.definitionCN: 住在某处，或以某建筑为住所、驻地
senses.example: The family occupies the upper floors of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人住在楼的上层。
senses.why: Living somewhere is holding it continuously. The legal phrase 'occupier' grew from exactly this: the person who is in possession of the property.
senses.whyCN: 住在某处就是持续地占住它。法律用语 occupier 正由此而来：实际占有该房产的人。

senses.title: Hold an office, post or rank
senses.titleCN: 担任职位：占住一个位置
senses.definition: to hold a job, office or official position
senses.definitionCN: 担任某项工作、职务或正式职位
senses.example: She occupies the chair of the department.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任系主任一职。
senses.why: A post is a place in an institution; whoever holds it fills that slot. The space sense turns social: the seat is taken by a person.
senses.whyCN: 职位是机构里的一个位置，谁担任就由谁填进那个格子。空间义转向社会意义：座位被人占住了。

senses.title: Occupy the mind: keep attention busy
senses.titleCN: 占据心思：让注意力忙个不停
senses.definition: to fill someone's thoughts or attention, especially for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 填满某人的思绪或注意力，尤指持续很久
senses.example: The question occupied him for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题盘踞在他心里好几周。
senses.why: Attention is another space. When a thought grips it, no other thought can get in, so occupy comes to mean 'absorb the mind'.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是另一种空间。当一个念头抓住它，别的念头就进不来，于是 occupy 表示“占据心思”。

senses.title: Military occupation: control without annexing
senses.titleCN: 军事占领：控制而不并入
senses.definition: to control a country or territory with armed force, usually without making it part of one's own state
senses.definitionCN: 以武力控制某国或某地区，通常不把它并入本国
senses.example: The army occupied the region for six years.
senses.exampleCN: 军队占领该地区六年。
senses.why: The oldest 'seize' sense scaled up to whole territories. Holding the ground is the point, and the legal status of the land is left open.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的“夺取”义放大到整片领土。要点在于握住土地，而土地的法律归属则悬置不论。

senses.title: Take a place in a ranking or order
senses.definition: to have or fill a particular place in a list, ranking or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在名单、排名或序列中占有某个位置
senses.example: The novel occupies third place on the bestseller list.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在畅销榜上位居第三。
senses.why: A rank is a numbered slot. The thing that holds that slot occupies it, even though nothing physical is gripped.
senses.whyCN: 名次是一个带编号的格子。占住该格子的东西就 occupy 它，尽管并没有任何实体被抓住。

senses.title: Occupy oneself: keep oneself busy
senses.titleCN: 使自己忙碌：给自己找事做
senses.definition: in the reflexive form occupy oneself with, to keep oneself busy with an activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于反身形式 occupy oneself with，表示让自己忙于某项活动
senses.example: He occupied himself with repairing the old clock.
senses.exampleCN: 他让自己忙着修那口旧钟。
senses.why: The reflexive turns the grip inward: instead of an outside thing holding you, you give your own time to an activity.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把“握”转向自身：不是外物抓住你，而是你把自己的时间交给一项活动。

senses.title: Archaic euphemism: have sex with
senses.titleCN: 古委婉语：与……发生性关系
senses.definition: in 16th and 17th century usage, a polite cover for having sexual intercourse with someone
senses.definitionCN: 在 16、17 世纪用法中，作为“与某人发生性关系”的委婉说法
senses.example: Renaissance writers used occupy as a discreet cover for a sexual act.
senses.exampleCN: 文艺复兴时期的作家用 occupy 隐晦地指代性行为。
senses.why: The 'take possession of a person' sense was pushed into sexual meaning in the early 15th century. Because of that, polite usage dropped the word for a time, and occupant could even mean a prostitute.
senses.whyCN: “占有一个人的身体”这一层在 15 世纪早期被推成性含义。正因如此，讲究礼貌的用法一度回避这个词，occupant 甚至可指妓女。

intro.en: Occupy arrived in English in the mid-14th century through Old French, from Latin occupare 'seize, take possession'. The ending is hard to explain, but the record is old; a 16th-17th century sexual euphemism later pushed the word out of polite use for a while.
intro.cn: occupy 于 14 世纪中期经古法语进入英语，来自拉丁语 occupare“夺取、占有”。词尾音节难以解释，但记录已很古老；16 至 17 世纪的性委婉义后来又使这个词一度退出礼貌用法。

items.en: Occupien is recorded meaning 'to take possession of and retain or keep'; the same period shows the senses 'fill space or time' and 'employ a person'.
items.cn: occupien 记录为“取得并保有、占住”；同一时期还出现“占据空间或时间”和“雇用某人”的义项。

items.en: Borrowed irregularly from Old French ocuper / occuper (13c.), or taken directly from Latin occupare.
items.cn: 不规则地借自古法语 ocuper / occuper（13 世纪），或直接取自拉丁语 occupare。

items.en: Latin occupare 'take over, seize, take into possession' is an emphatic form of ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp, seize'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 occupare“接管、夺取、占为己有”是 ob“覆于其上”加 capere“抓、夺”的强调形式。

items.en: Capere goes back to PIE *kap- 'to grasp', the root behind captive and capture as well.
items.cn: capere 追溯到原始印欧语 *kap-“抓”，captive 与 capture 也出自这个词根。

items.en: The sense 'have sexual intercourse with' is found from the early 15th century and served as a euphemism in the 16th and 17th centuries; Shakespeare uses it in Henry IV, Part 2, and occupant could then mean a prostitute.
items.cn: “与……发生性关系”义自 15 世纪早期可见，16、17 世纪成为委婉语；莎士比亚在《亨利四世下篇》用过它，当时的 occupant 还可指妓女。

items.en: Modern English keeps the neutral senses of holding space, time, office and attention, and forms occupation, occupant and occupancy from the same stem.
items.cn: 现代英语保留占据空间、时间、职位与注意力等中性义，并由同一词干构成 occupation、occupant、occupancy。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to happen or come to mind. It shares the ob- beginning but comes from currere 'to run', not from capere 'to seize'.
entries.definitionCN: 发生；想到。它同样以 ob- 开头，但词根是 currere“跑”，不是 capere“抓”。

entries.definition: a person who lives in or uses a place. It is the noun built on occupy, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 居住者；占用者。它是 occupy 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: absorbed in one's own thoughts. The pre- 'before' adds the idea of the mind being taken up in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 心事重重的；出神的。pre-“预先”加了“心思先被占去”的意思。

entries.definition: to take hold of something suddenly and by force. It stresses the grab, while occupy stresses keeping possession.
entries.definitionCN: 突然用力抓住。它强调抓的动作，occupy 强调占住不放。

entries.definition: to live in a place as its population. It is used of people and animals, while occupy can also mean simply filling space.
entries.definitionCN: 作为居民住在某地。它多用于人和动物，occupy 也可仅指占据空间。

entries.definition: to attract and hold someone's interest. It focuses on the attraction, while occupy focuses on the attention being filled up.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引并保持某人的兴趣。它侧重吸引力，occupy 侧重注意力被填满。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin ob plus capere, the capere family in capture and captive, and the modern nouns occupation and occupant.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + capere，capture 与 captive 中的 capere 词族，以及现代名词 occupation 与 occupant。

normal.en: ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp' gives 'grasp over something': the hand closes on it and holds.
normal.cn: ob“覆于其上”加 capere“抓”就是“在上面抓住”：手合拢握住不放。

normal.en: Capture and captive share the same capere root, so all three words are about a grip that does not let go.
normal.cn: capture 与 captive 同出 capere，因此这三个词都围绕“握住不放”。

normal.en: Obtain uses tenere 'to hold', occur uses currere 'to run': same ob- prefix, three different roots.
normal.cn: obtain 用 tenere“握持”，occur 用 currere“跑”：同一个 ob- 前缀，三个不同词根。

normal.en: Occupation is both a job and a military takeover, because both are a held place.
normal.cn: occupation 既是职业也是军事占领，因为两者都是“占住的位置”。

normal.en: Occupy oneself with is the reflexive branch: you give your own time to a task.
normal.cn: occupy oneself with 是反身分支：你把自己的时间交给一项任务。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed flat on a table: the table under it is no longer free, and that is occupy in one gesture.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌平压在桌面上：掌下的桌面不再空着，这就是 occupy 的一个动作。

abstract.en: The same hand can close on a building, an afternoon, a chair, a rank, or a thought.
abstract.cn: 同一只手可以握住一栋楼、一个下午、一把椅子、一个名次或一个念头。

abstract.en: When the grip turns inward, the hand holds its own time: that is occupy oneself.
abstract.cn: 当这只手握向自身，它握的是自己的时间：这就是 occupy oneself。

examples.en: A single bookshelf occupied the entire wall of the small study.
examples.cn: 一个书架占满了小书房整面墙。

examples.en: Rebuilding the harbour occupied the town for three summers.
examples.cn: 重建港口让全镇忙了三个夏天。

examples.en: The reporter was occupied with verifying the source and missed the call.
examples.cn: 记者正忙着核实消息来源，错过了那通电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥 Q 派」——奥 Q 派的人一进门就占了整间会议室 → occupy 占据、占用

root: 源自拉丁语 occupare“夺取、占有”= ob-“覆于其上、对着”+ capere“抓、夺”（PIE *kap-“抓”），核心是“抓住并占住不放”；词尾音节来源难以解释。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of occupy all start from one gesture: a hand closes over something and holds it. The same grip then measures floors, hours, homes, posts, ranks, attention and, in the oldest branch, whole territories.
sensesIntro.cn: occupy 的十个义项都从同一个动作出发：手合拢抓住某物并握住。同一只握持之手随后量出地板、小时、住所、职位、名次、注意力，以及最古老分支里的整片领土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing over something and holding it tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢抓住某物，紧紧握住不放。

branches.en: SEIZURE: taking a thing or a whole territory by force and keeping control of it.
branches.cn: 夺取：以武力拿下一件东西或整片领土，并保持控制。

branches.en: SPACE, TIME AND HOME: the grip becomes the floor a thing covers, the hours an activity uses, and the house a family lives in.
branches.cn: 空间、时间与住所：握持变成物体覆盖的地面、活动用掉的时间，以及一家人居住的房子。

branches.en: POSITION: a post or a rank is a slot in an institution or a list, and its holder fills that slot.
branches.cn: 位置：职位或名次是机构或名单中的格子，担任者把它填满。

branches.en: BUSY MIND: attention can be gripped from outside, or handed over by oneself in the reflexive form.
branches.cn: 忙碌的心神：注意力既可以被外物抓住，也可以在反身形式里由自己交出。

branches.en: THE OLD EUPHEMISM: possessing a person was pushed into sexual meaning, a branch polite usage later abandoned.
branches.cn: 旧委婉语：“占有人”被推成性含义，这一分支后来被礼貌用法弃用。

intro.en: Occupy is Latin ob- 'over, against' plus capere 'to grasp', with the verb ending -are. English keeps the stem occup- and builds nouns with -ation, -ant, -ancy and -ier.
intro.cn: occupy 由拉丁语 ob-“覆于其上、对着”加 capere“抓”和动词词尾 -are 构成。英语保留词干 occup-，并用 -ation、-ant、-ancy、-ier 造名词。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin occupare, an emphatic compound of ob and capere; capere 'to grasp' is the root at the centre.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 occupare，即 ob 与 capere 的强调复合词；中心的词根是 capere“抓”。

items.meaning: to seize and hold; to fill space, time or attention
items.example: Two guards occupy the gate at all times.
items.exampleCN: 两名卫兵始终守着大门。

items.meaning: a person who lives in or uses a place
items.meaningCN: 居住者；占用者；乘坐者（-ant 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The new occupant moved in last Friday.
items.exampleCN: 新住户上周五搬了进来。

items.meaning: the state of being occupied; the rate of use
items.meaningCN: 占用；居住；入住率（-ancy 构成状态名词）
items.example: Hotel occupancy falls sharply in winter.
items.exampleCN: 旅馆入住率在冬季大幅下降。

items.meaning: a job; the act of taking control of a place
items.meaningCN: 职业；占领；占用（-ation 构成行为或状态名词）
items.exampleCN: 她把自己的职业填作“译者”。

items.meaning: relating to a job or the workplace
items.meaningCN: 职业的；职业引起的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Noise is a common occupational hazard in factories.
items.exampleCN: 噪音是工厂里常见的职业危害。

items.meaning: the person who occupies a property or territory
items.example: The occupier of the flat is responsible for repairs.
items.exampleCN: 该公寓的住户负责维修。

items.meaning: absorbed in one's own thoughts; already taken up
items.meaningCN: 心事重重的；专注的（pre-“预先”+ occupy，心思先被占去）
items.example: He was too preoccupied to notice the rain.
items.exampleCN: 他心事太重，没注意到下雨。

items.meaning: a thought or subject that fills the mind
items.meaningCN: 全神贯注的事；心头大事
items.exampleCN: 安全成了他心头最挂念的事。

items.structure: capt- (grasp, from capere) + -ure (noun and verb ending)
items.meaning: to take by force or to record an image
items.example: The camera captured the whole scene.

items.meaningCN: 被关押的；俘虏（同一“抓”词根）
items.example: The captive birds were released at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 被关的鸟在黎明时被放走了。

latinEntries.meaning: to take over, seize, take into possession

definition_zh: 法官；裁判；判断；评判
definition_en: a person who decides cases in court or scores a contest, or to form an opinion about something after thinking
core_image: 一个人坐在高台后，手里握着木槌，眼前是两方对立的说法
scene: 法庭里所有人都安静下来，高台上的那个人翻开卷宗说了第一句话。 The judge asked the witness to speak more slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 judge 是「法官」（第 1 个义项：法庭上作出裁决的人），句意为法官请证人说得慢一些。画面里的物件：木槌、卷宗、高台。

collocations.phrase: as far as I can judge

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「判断；判决」
同源于 judex 词干的形容词，义为「司法的」
加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「误判」
同带 judic- 词根的形近词，义为「偏见」

senses.title: Person in a court
senses.definition: the official who hears a case and decides it according to law
senses.definitionCN: 审理案件并依法裁决的官员
senses.example: The judge gave him a fine and a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 法官判他罚款并给予警告。
senses.why: The formal sense is the oldest and still the defining one.
senses.whyCN: 正式义最古老，至今仍是这个词的定型义。

senses.title: Person who scores a contest
senses.definition: a person who decides the result of a competition
senses.definitionCN: 决定比赛结果的人
senses.example: One judge gave the singer full marks.
senses.exampleCN: 有一位评委给这位歌手打了满分。
senses.why: The same Latin compound covered any declared verdict, including a panel of scorers.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁复合词也涵盖任何宣告的裁决，包括评委打分。

senses.title: Forming an opinion
senses.definition: to reach a conclusion about someone or something after thought
senses.definitionCN: 经过思考对人或事得出结论
senses.example: Do not judge the plan until you see the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 没看到数字之前先别评判这个方案。
senses.why: Everyday English dropped the courtroom and kept the weighing of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 日常英语丢掉了法庭，只留下权衡证据这一层。

senses.title: Deciding a case
senses.definition: to hear evidence and give a legal decision
senses.definitionCN: 听取证据并作出法律裁决
senses.example: The court will judge the case next month.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下个月审理此案。
senses.why: The verb sense is the noun turned around: to act the part of the judge.
senses.whyCN: 动词义是名词的翻转：去充当法官这个角色。

intro.en: Judge comes from Latin judex, built from jus "law" and dicere "to say": the one who says the law.
intro.cn: judge 来自拉丁语 judex，由 jus「法」与 dicere「说」构成：说出法律的人。

items.en: jus or ius meant "law, right".
items.cn: jus 或 ius 意为「法、权利」。

items.en: dicere meant "to say, to declare".
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、宣告」。

items.en: judex joined them: the one who declares the law.
items.cn: judex 把两者合起来：宣告法律的人。

items.en: French turned judex into juge.
items.cn: 法语把 judex 变成 juge。

items.en: English spelt it judge and extended it to any opinion.
items.cn: 英语写作 judge，并把词义扩展到任何意见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jud- root; the near-meaning group holds words for deciding and evaluating.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jud- 词根；近义组收表示裁定与评价的词。

entries.definition: The act of forming an opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「判断」，同族词。

entries.definition: Relating to courts of law.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「司法的」，同词根。

entries.definition: An opinion formed without evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「偏见」，同词根加 pre-。

entries.definition: To estimate the quality or size of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「评估」，偏测量。

entries.definition: To decide the value of something carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「评价」，偏价值。

entries.definition: The official who controls a match.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「裁判」，多用于球赛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into law plus say.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它拆成「法」加「说」。

normal.en: jus means law and dicere means say.
normal.cn: jus 是法，dicere 是说。

normal.en: A judge is the one who says the law out loud.
normal.cn: judge 就是把法律当场说出来的人。

normal.en: A referee judges a match; a judge tries a case.
normal.cn: referee 判比赛，judge 审案子。

normal.en: To judge is to give a verdict in your own mind.
normal.cn: judge 作动词，就是在心里下一个结论。

normal.en: Add -ment and you have the verdict itself.
normal.cn: 加 -ment 就得到判决本身。

abstract.en: A judge is a voice that the law speaks through.
abstract.cn: 法官是法律借来说话的那个嗓子。

abstract.en: Judging people is cheap; judging fairly is not.
abstract.cn: 评判别人很便宜，公平地评判不是。

abstract.en: Every judgement leaves a door open to appeal.
abstract.cn: 每一个判断都留着一扇上诉的门。

examples.en: The judge listened to both sides before speaking.
examples.cn: 法官先听完双方才开口。

examples.en: Three judges scored the final dance.
examples.cn: 三位评委为决赛的舞蹈打分。

examples.en: You cannot judge a book by a single page.
examples.cn: 不能只看一页就评判一本书。

dict_mnemonic.text: jus（法）+ dic（说）——把法律说出来的人

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」+ dicere「说」→ judex「宣告法律者」→ 古法语 juge → 英语 judge。同族有 judgement、judicial、prejudice、justice。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a court judge, a contest judge, forming an opinion, and trying a case.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：法庭法官、比赛裁判、形成判断，以及审理案件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone seated above two contrary claims with a gavel.
core.cn: 核心意象：在高处握着木槌、面对两种相反说法的人。

branches.en: THE BENCH: the court side, where a case is decided.
branches.cn: 审判席这条线：裁决案件的法庭一面。

branches.en: THE SCORE: the contest side, where marks are given.
branches.cn: 打分这条线：给出分数的一方。

branches.en: THE MIND: the everyday side, where opinions form.
branches.cn: 头脑这条线：日常形成看法的这一面。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: formal rulings and private opinions share a shape.
branches.cn: 权威这条线：正式裁决与私下看法形状相同。

branches.en: THE STANDARD: both senses need a measure to compare against.
branches.cn: 标准这条线：两个义项都需要一把衡量的尺。

intro.en: Judge is Latin jus "law" plus the root dic- "say", worn down through French.
intro.cn: judge 是拉丁语 jus「法」加词根 dic-「说」，再经法语磨短而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin jus, dicere and judex are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jus、dicere 与 judex 均有记载。

items.example: The root also appears in judicial and prejudice.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 judicial 与 prejudice。

items.example: The root also appears in dictate and predict.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 dictate 与 predict。

definition_zh: 文件；档案；归档；排队行进
definition_en: a folder or set of papers, a collection of stored information, to store papers in order, or to walk in a line
core_image: 一叠纸被一根细线穿在一起，挂在墙上的钉子上
scene: 他打开文件，读起第一页。 He opened the file and read the first page.
sceneCN: 这里 file 是「文件」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他打开文件，读起第一页。

derivatives.zh: 归档；文件
归档人
文件名

senses.title: Document
senses.definition: a set of papers or data kept together
senses.definitionCN: 归在一起的一组纸质或电子资料
senses.example: He opened the file and read the first page.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开文件，读起第一页。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a document.
senses.whyCN: 这是文件最常见的意思。

senses.title: Stored record
senses.definition: a collection of records kept for reference
senses.definitionCN: 供查阅的档案记录
senses.example: The police keep the case on file.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把此案存档。
senses.why: Records are kept in a file for later use.
senses.whyCN: 记录被存进档案以备日后使用。

senses.title: To store in order
senses.definition: to put papers into a system or place
senses.definitionCN: 把文件放入系统或位置
senses.example: File the reports before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 周五前把报告归档。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of keeping it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为保存它的动作。

senses.title: To walk in line
senses.definition: to walk one behind another
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个地走
senses.example: The children filed into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排队走进大厅。
senses.why: A line of people resembles a string of papers.
senses.whyCN: 一列人就像一串文件。

intro.en: File comes from Latin filum, a thread, because papers were once strung on a line.
intro.cn: file 出自拉丁语 filum（线），因为旧时文件被穿在线上。

items.en: Filum meant a thread or string.
items.cn: filum 意为线或细绳。

items.en: Filare meant to spin thread.
items.cn: filare 意为纺线。

items.en: Filer meant to string papers on a line.
items.cn: filer 意为把文件穿在线上。

items.en: A file became a set of papers kept in order.
items.cn: file 变成按顺序保存的一组文件。

items.en: The word extended to computer files.
items.cn: 该词扩展到计算机文件。

note.en: File is compared with similar-looking words and with words for stored records.

entries.definition: to make something full

entries.definition: past tense of file

entries.definition: the act of storing papers

entries.definition: a written record
entries.definitionCN: 文件

entries.definition: stored information
entries.definitionCN: 记录

entries.definition: a cover for papers
entries.definitionCN: 文件夹

normalIntro.en: File is a thread of papers, a stored record, and a line of people.
normalIntro.cn: file 是一串纸、一份存档，也是一列人。

normal.en: Keep the contract on file.
normal.cn: 把合同存档。

normal.en: She filed the letters by date.
normal.cn: 她按日期给信件归档。

normal.en: The students walked in single file.
normal.cn: 学生们排成一列行走。

normal.en: A filename names a computer file.
normal.cn: 文件名给电脑文件命名。

normal.en: File a complaint means to report it formally.
normal.cn: file a complaint 意为正式提出投诉。

abstract.en: A thread can hold many pages into one story.
abstract.cn: 一根线能把许多页穿成一个故事。

abstract.en: Order is what turns paper into a file.
abstract.cn: 秩序把纸张变成档案。

abstract.en: A line of people moves at the speed of its first step.
abstract.cn: 一列人的速度取决于第一步。

examples.en: He opened the file and read the first page.
examples.cn: 他打开文件，读起第一页。

examples.en: The police keep the case on file.
examples.cn: 警方把此案存档。

examples.en: The children filed into the hall.
examples.cn: 孩子们排队走进大厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: file 出自拉丁语 filum（线），本义「把文件穿在线上保存」，后引申为文件、档案与排队行进。

root: 源自拉丁语 filum（线），核心义「用线串起、成序保存」。

sensesIntro.en: File means a document, a stored record, the act of storing, or walking in a line.
sensesIntro.cn: file 意为文件、档案、归档或排队行进。

core.en: Papers held together in order.
core.cn: 按顺序归拢在一起的纸张。

branches.en: Papers kept together.
branches.cn: 归在一起的文件。

branches.en: Records kept for later use.
branches.cn: 留待日后查阅的档案。

branches.en: The act of putting papers away.
branches.cn: 把文件收起来的行为。

branches.en: People moving one behind another.
branches.cn: 一个跟一个前进的人。

branches.cn: 一份文件与一宗案卷共用一个词。

intro.en: File belongs to the Latin thread family, from which profile and filament also come.

definition_zh: 轻敲；轻拍；水龙头；开发；利用
definition_en: to hit something lightly, a device controlling water flow, or to make use of a resource
core_image: 指尖在桌面上轻轻敲三下
scene: 有人轻轻敲了敲车窗，提醒他绿灯亮了。 Someone tapped gently on the car window to remind him the light was green.
sceneCN: 这里 tap 是「轻敲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：有人轻轻敲了敲车窗，提醒他绿灯亮了。

derivatives.zh: 轻敲者
轻敲；窃听

senses.title: To hit lightly
senses.definition: to strike something gently with the fingers or a small object
senses.definitionCN: 用手指或小物件轻轻击打
senses.example: Someone tapped gently on the car window.
senses.exampleCN: 有人轻轻敲了敲车窗。
senses.why: The sound of a light blow is the oldest core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 轻击发出的声音是这个词最古老的内核。

senses.title: A device for running water
senses.definition: a device that controls the flow of water from a pipe
senses.definitionCN: 控制管道中水流大小的装置
senses.example: The tap in the kitchen kept dripping all night.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的水龙头整夜滴水。
senses.why: A faucet was once a plug struck or turned to release water.
senses.whyCN: 水龙头最初就是被敲开或拧开的塞子，动作延伸成了器具。

senses.title: To make use of a resource
senses.definition: to make use of something that is available
senses.definitionCN: 把已有的资源拿出来使用
senses.example: The company tapped into a young market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司开发了一个年轻的市场。
senses.why: Opening a tap lets stored water flow, just as a resource is opened for use.
senses.whyCN: 打开龙头让存水流出，正如把资源打开来使用。

intro.en: Tap began as the sound and act of a light blow, then named a water outlet.
intro.cn: tap 最初是轻击的声音与动作，后来指水的出口。

items.en: Tappen meant to strike lightly.
items.cn: tappen 意为轻敲。

items.en: Tap named the strike and its sound.
items.cn: tap 指轻击及其声音。

items.en: A tap became a spout for water.
items.cn: tap 又指放水的龙头。

items.en: Tapping a line meant listening secretly.
items.cn: 在线上「搭一下」就是秘密窃听。

items.en: To tap a resource is to open it for use.
items.cn: 开发资源就是把它打开使用。

note.en: Tap is compared with look-alike words and with words for knocking and faucets.
note.cn: 把 tap 与形近词以及表示敲击和水龙头的词作对比。

entries.definition: the pointed end
entries.definitionCN: 尖端；只拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the highest part
entries.definitionCN: 顶部；只拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: one who taps
entries.definitionCN: 轻敲者

entries.definition: to hit a door to be let in
entries.definitionCN: 敲

entries.definition: to touch gently with a flat hand
entries.definitionCN: 轻拍

entries.definition: an American word for a tap
entries.definitionCN: 水龙头

normalIntro.en: Tap is a small sound, a small turn of a handle, and a resource let loose.
normalIntro.cn: tap 是轻轻一声、轻轻一拧，也是让资源流出来。

normal.en: Someone tapped gently on the car window.
normal.cn: 有人轻轻敲了敲车窗。

normal.en: The kitchen tap kept dripping.
normal.cn: 厨房水龙头一直在滴水。

normal.en: The company tapped into a young market.
normal.cn: 这家公司开发了一个年轻的市场。

normal.en: He tapped the keys twice.
normal.cn: 他轻敲了两下键盘。

normal.en: Tap water is safe to drink here.
normal.cn: 这里的自来水可以直接喝。

abstract.en: A light touch opens a heavy flow.
abstract.cn: 轻轻一触，放出滔滔水流。

abstract.en: Tapping is asking for attention in sound.
abstract.cn: 轻敲是用声音请求注意。

abstract.en: Every resource waits behind a tap.
abstract.cn: 每份资源都等在某个龙头后面。

examples.en: Someone tapped gently on the car window to remind him the light was green.
examples.cn: 有人轻轻敲了敲车窗，提醒他绿灯亮了。

examples.en: The tap in the kitchen kept dripping all night.
examples.cn: 厨房的水龙头整夜滴水。

examples.en: The company tapped into a young market.
examples.cn: 这家公司开发了一个年轻的市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踏普」——脚尖「踏」着地打拍子，一下一下，就是轻敲。

root: 中古英语 tappen（轻击），拟声来源；由轻击动作引申出水龙头与「开发资源」。

sensesIntro.en: Tap grows from a light blow to a water outlet to the opening of any resource.
sensesIntro.cn: tap 从轻击长出水龙头，又长出「打开资源」的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingertips striking a surface three times.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖在表面上敲三下。

branches.en: The light blow is the source sense.
branches.cn: 轻击是源义项。

branches.en: The outlet releases what is stored.
branches.cn: 龙头释放储存之物。

branches.en: Resources flow like water.
branches.cn: 资源像水一样流出。

branches.en: Both are about opening a flow.
branches.cn: 两者都关于打开流动。

branches.en: Even a phone tap begins with a light touch.
branches.cn: 连电话窃听也始于轻轻一接。

intro.en: Tap builds a small family of agents and actions.
intro.cn: tap 构成由施动者与动作组成的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Tap is likely imitative in origin; Latin tangere, to touch, is only a semantic echo.
latinIntro.cn: tap 很可能是拟声词；拉丁语 tangere（触碰）只是语义回声。
