definition_zh: 诗歌（总称）；诗艺；诗意；韵文
definition_en: poems considered as a whole, as a form of literature; also the art of writing them, the quality of beauty they carry, and verse as a medium opposed to prose
core_image: 书架上并排立着许多薄薄的诗集，翻开的一页字句稀疏，空白比墨迹更多
scene: 雨夜的图书馆里只剩翻页的轻响，靠窗的桌上摊着一本薄薄的诗集。 She read poetry aloud to the empty room, pausing after every line.
sceneCN: 这里 poetry 指「诗歌」这个整体（第 1 个义项：作为文学体裁的诗歌总称，不可数，与可数的 poem 相对）；句意为她对着空房间朗读诗歌，每读完一行就停一停。图中可辨识物件：翻开的诗集、窗上的雨痕、台灯。

pos.zh: 诗歌（总称）；诗艺；诗意；韵文

forms.label: 不可数名词，通常无复数

derivatives.zh: 同源词，去掉集合词尾 -ry 后指写诗的人
同源词，指一首具体的诗，可数，与不可数的 poetry 分工不同
由希腊词干 poie- 加 -tic 构成，义为「诗的；富有诗意的」
由 poetic 加 -s 构成，义为「诗学」

senses.title: Poems considered as a whole
senses.definition: poems taken together as a body of writing and as a form of literature, used as an uncountable noun
senses.definitionCN: 把诗作作为一个整体来看的文学体裁，作不可数名词使用
senses.example: Her shelf holds more poetry than fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 她书架上的诗集比小说还多。
senses.why: The -ry ending that English took from French marks a collectivity, so poetry gathers many separate poems into one mass and therefore takes no plural.
senses.whyCN: 英语从法语借来的 -ry 词尾表示集合，于是 poetry 把许多首独立的诗收成一个整体，因此没有复数形式。

senses.title: The art of writing poems
senses.definition: the craft of composing verse, including rhythm, line breaks and image
senses.definitionCN: 写作诗句的手艺，包括节奏、分行与意象
senses.example: He studied the poetry of the eighteenth century as a craft rather than a mood.
senses.exampleCN: 他把十八世纪的诗当作一门手艺来研究，而不是当作一种情绪。
senses.why: Latin poesis named the making before it named the made thing, so the craft sense is the older one rather than a later metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poesis 先指「制作」这个动作，再指做成的东西，所以「诗艺」义其实更早，并不是后来的比喻。

senses.title: A quality of beauty or feeling
senses.definition: a quality in a place, an action or an object that stirs feeling the way a poem does
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、动作或物件身上那种像诗一样打动人的品质
senses.example: There is poetry in the way a fishing boat turns back at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在黄昏掉头回港的样子，自有一种诗意。
senses.why: Once the word meant the crafted arrangement of words, it could be lent to any arrangement of things that moves a person in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词曾指对词语的精心安排，它就可以被借去形容任何能同样打动人的事物安排。

senses.title: Verse as a medium, opposed to prose
senses.definition: language shaped by rhythm and line rather than by the ordinary order of sentences
senses.definitionCN: 由节奏与分行塑形、而非依照普通句子顺序排列的语言
senses.example: The story shifts from prose into poetry in its final pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事在最后几页从散文转成了诗体。
senses.why: A poem is recognised first by its shape on the page and in the ear, so poetry also names the medium itself, set against prose.
senses.whyCN: 诗最先被人认出的是它在纸面上和耳朵里的形态，所以 poetry 也指这种媒介本身，与散文相对。

intro.en: Poetry and poet share one Greek stem, but poetry took a collective ending and settled as the uncountable name of the whole art.
intro.cn: poetry 与 poet 共用一个希腊词干，但 poetry 接了集合词尾，固定为指整门艺术而不可数的名称。

items.en: The verb poiein meant to make or compose, the ordinary word for producing anything.
items.cn: 动词 poiein 意为制作、编写，是制作任何东西时最普通的说法。

items.en: The noun poiēsis named a making or a composition, and could be used of the making of a poem.
items.cn: 名词 poiēsis 指制作或作品，也可以用来指一首诗的作成。

items.en: Latin used poesis for verse and poeta for the writer; both were learned borrowings from Greek.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 poesis 指诗，用 poeta 指写诗的人，两者都是从希腊语借来的学术词。

items.en: Old French poetrie, also written poeterie, named both the art and the collected verse, with a suffix that marks a body of things.
items.cn: 古法语 poetrie（也写作 poeterie）既指这门艺术，也指收集起来的诗作，词尾本身带有「一批事物」的集合意味。

items.en: English poetry settled as the uncountable term for the whole field, leaving poem as the countable word for one work.
items.cn: 英语 poetry 固定为指整个领域的不可数词，而单篇作品留给可数的 poem。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same making family, where the countable unit and the adjective sit beside the collective noun; the near-meaning group gathers other words of the verse trade.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个「制作」词族，可数单位与形容词都挨着这个集合名词；近义组收诗歌行当里的其他词。

entries.definition: One single piece of verse, countable, the unit that the collective noun gathers.
entries.definitionCN: 单篇诗作，可数，正是集合名词所收的单位。

entries.definition: Of verse, or having the beauty associated with it.
entries.definitionCN: 诗体的；富有诗意的。

entries.definition: The person who makes poems; the collective noun adds its ending to the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 写诗的人；集合名词是在同一词干上加词尾而成。

entries.definition: The theory or systematic study of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 诗学；对诗歌的系统研究。

entries.definition: Writing arranged in lines, usually with rhythm; also a single line.
entries.definitionCN: 分行写成的文字，通常有节奏；也可指一行诗。

entries.definition: Ordinary written language without line breaks, the counterpart of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 不按诗行排列的普通书面语，与韵文相对。

entries.definition: The matching of sounds at the ends of lines.
entries.definitionCN: 诗行末尾音韵相合。

entries.definition: A short poem of personal feeling, often meant to be sung.
entries.definitionCN: 表达个人情感的短诗，常可歌唱。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek noun of making with a collective ending, and that ending is the whole difference between one poem and the art itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带集合词尾的希腊「制作」名词，而这个词尾正是一首诗与整门艺术之间的全部差别。

normal.en: Poetry shares its stem with poet, but the -ry ending turns a person into a whole field of work.
normal.cn: poetry 与 poet 共用词干，但 -ry 词尾把一个人变成了一整片工作领域。

normal.en: Poem is the countable unit and poetry is the uncountable mass, so we say a poem but never a poetry.
normal.cn: poem 是可数的单位，poetry 是不可数的整体，所以说 a poem，却不说 a poetry。

normal.en: Greek poiēsis meant a making, which is why poetry can name the craft and not only the finished texts.
normal.cn: 希腊语 poiēsis 意为制作，所以 poetry 既能指手艺，也能指成品。

normal.en: Poetic keeps the adjective ending -ic and describes the quality, while poetry names the thing itself.
normal.cn: poetic 保留形容词词尾 -ic 来描述性质，poetry 则指事物本身。

normal.en: The plural poems is normal for separate works, but poetry stays singular even when it covers centuries.
normal.cn: 分开的作品用复数 poems 很正常，而 poetry 即使涵盖几个世纪也仍是单数。

abstract.en: A language that keeps a separate uncountable word for verse is treating poems as a substance rather than a list.
abstract.cn: 一种语言若为诗保留一个独立的不可数词，就是把诗当成一种物质，而不是一份清单。

abstract.en: The same word covers a craft and a feeling, which suggests that technique and emotion were never meant to be separated here.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指手艺又指感受，这说明在这个领域里技巧与情感从来不该被分开。

abstract.en: Saying there is poetry in a harbour is a quiet claim that the world can be arranged like a line.
abstract.cn: 说一个港湾里有诗意，是在轻声主张：世界也可以像一行诗那样被安排。

examples.en: She writes poetry in the mornings before work.
examples.cn: 她在上班前的早晨写诗。

examples.en: The anthology traces four centuries of Chinese poetry.
examples.cn: 这部选集梳理了中国诗歌四百年的脉络。

examples.en: There was a strange poetry in the empty station at midnight.
examples.cn: 午夜空旷的车站里有一种奇特的诗意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖厄特里」——把一首诗剖开，里面是一层层的节奏、分行与意象。

root: 希腊语 poiein（制作）→ poiēsis（制作、诗作）→ 拉丁语 poesis（借自希腊语）→ 古法语 poetrie（诗艺、诗作）→ 英语 poetry；词尾 -ry 表集合。

sensesIntro.en: The core is verse taken as a whole; the senses divide into the craft, the feeling it leaves behind, and the medium that stands against prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是作为整体的诗；义项分为这门手艺、它留下的感受，以及与散文相对的媒介。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin volumes standing side by side on a shelf, an open page with wide margins where the white space speaks as much as the ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：书架上并排立着薄薄的诗集，翻开的一页留白很宽，空白几乎和墨迹一样在说话。

branches.en: a shelf where thin volumes outnumber novels
branches.cn: 书架上薄薄的诗集比小说还多

branches.en: a hand counting beats while shaping a line
branches.cn: 一只手打着拍子把一行字排好

branches.en: a harbour at dusk that feels like a stanza
branches.cn: 黄昏的港湾像一节诗

branches.en: a page breaking from paragraphs into lines
branches.cn: 页面从成段文字断成一行行

branches.en: one word for printed books and for a feeling in the air
branches.cn: 同一个词既指印成的书，也指空气里的感受

intro.en: A Greek verb of making, its noun of process, a Latin loan and a French collective ending all meet in this one word.
intro.cn: 一个表示制作的希腊动词、它的过程名词、一个拉丁借词和一个法语集合词尾，在这一个词里汇合。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 希腊语名词词尾：动作、过程

items.meaning: the art and body of verse

items.meaningCN: 集合后缀：一批事物或一门技艺

definition_zh: 麻袋；口袋；一袋之量；解雇（英，非正式）；掠夺（古）
definition_en: a large bag made of rough material, the amount a sack holds, or to dismiss someone from a job
core_image: 一只粗布大口袋：装得下粮食，也装得下「卷铺盖走人」的行囊
scene: 农民把刚收获的土豆装进麻袋扛回谷仓。 The farmer carried a heavy sack of potatoes into the barn.
sceneCN: 这里 sack 是「麻袋」（第 1 个义项：粗材料做成的大口袋）；句意：农民扛着一袋沉甸甸的土豆走进谷仓。

pos.zh: 麻袋；一袋之量；（英，非正式）解雇

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 转名词，义为「麻袋布；粗麻布」
由 sack 加 -ful 后缀构成，义为「一袋的量」

senses.title: A large rough bag
senses.definition: a large bag made of strong rough cloth or paper, used for storing and carrying things
senses.definitionCN: 用粗布或厚纸做成的大袋子，用于储存和搬运
senses.example: He tied the top of the sack with a rope.
senses.exampleCN: 他用绳子把麻袋口扎紧。
senses.why: A big open bag that swallows grain whole is the oldest picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一口吞下整袋粮食的大开口布袋，是这个词最古老的画面。

senses.title: The amount a sack holds
senses.definition: the amount that a sack contains, used as a measure
senses.definitionCN: 麻袋所容纳的量，用作计量
senses.example: The shop sells flour by the sack.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店按袋出售面粉。
senses.why: A container lends its name to whatever quantity fills it.
senses.whyCN: 容器之名顺势指称它所盛装的量。

senses.title: To dismiss from a job
senses.definition: to dismiss someone from their job, used in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 英式非正式用语，指把人从职位上辞退
senses.example: He got the sack for being late again.
senses.exampleCN: 他因再次迟到而被炒了鱿鱼。
senses.why: A dismissed worker packs his belongings into a bag and carries it away.
senses.whyCN: 被辞退的工人把私物装进布袋拎走，「卷铺盖」成了「解雇」的代称。

senses.title: To plunder a town
senses.definition: to loot and destroy a captured town, an older literary use
senses.definitionCN: 旧式书面用法，指攻陷城镇后劫掠破坏
senses.example: Historians describe how the enemy sacked the ancient city.
senses.exampleCN: 史书记载敌军如何洗劫了那座古城。
senses.why: Soldiers emptied a town the way one empties a sack, turning everything out.
senses.whyCN: 士兵清空城镇如同倒空一只麻袋，把一切倾倒出来。

intro.en: Sack comes through Old French from Latin saccus, from Greek sakkos, a bag of coarse cloth.
intro.cn: sack 经古法语来自拉丁语 saccus，词根为希腊语 sakkos（粗布袋）。

items.en: Sakkos in Greek meant a bag or loose cloak of coarse cloth.
items.cn: 希腊语 sakkos 指粗布袋或宽松粗布外套，一般认为是词族源头。

items.en: Latin took the word as saccus, keeping the bag meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 saccus，袋义不变。

items.en: Old French carried it as sac into England with the Norman Conquest.
items.cn: 古法语承袭为 sac，随诺曼征服进入英格兰。

items.en: Sack meant the bag, the quantity, and by the seventeenth century the plundering of towns.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 sack 兼指口袋与袋量，十七世纪又添「洗劫城镇」义。

items.en: Get the sack arose from workmen carrying their tools home in a bag when dismissed.
items.cn: 十九世纪英国工人被辞退时把工具装袋带回家，get the sack 由此成为「被解雇」的习语。

note.en: Sack has look-alike family words and near-meaning words about bags and dismissal.
note.cn: sack 的形近词多属同族，近义词集中在袋子与解雇义场。

entries.definition: rough cloth used for making sacks
entries.definitionCN: 麻袋布；粗麻布，sack 的派生词

entries.definition: the amount a sack holds
entries.definitionCN: 一袋的量，sack 加 -ful 的派生词

entries.definition: a small meal eaten between main meals
entries.definitionCN: 零食；点心，与 sack 仅差首字母，词源无关，只是形近

entries.definition: a container of soft material with handles or an opening
entries.definitionCN: 袋子；提包，泛指一切软质容器，sack 特指粗大麻袋

entries.definition: to dismiss someone from a job
entries.definitionCN: 解雇（英式口语），与 sack 同义，fire 更常用于美式英语

entries.definition: to steal goods from a place by force
entries.definitionCN: 劫掠；抢夺，与 sack 的旧义相近，但强调抢夺而非攻城

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember sack through bags and bad news.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕口袋与坏消息的记忆路径。

normal.en: SACK rhymes with PACK: pack things into a sack.
normal.cn: SACK 与 PACK 押韵：把东西 pack 进 sack 里。

normal.en: A sack race: hop inside a big bag and jump.
normal.cn: 麻袋赛跑：钻进大布袋里蹦跳前进。

normal.en: Hit the sack means hit the bed: sleep time.
normal.cn: hit the sack 意为上床：去和枕头「打交道」。

normal.en: Get the sack: your belongings leave in the same bag.
normal.cn: get the sack：被解雇时，私物还是装进那只布袋带走。

normal.en: One sack of rice feeds a family for weeks.
normal.cn: 一袋大米够一家人吃上好几个星期。

abstract.en: Picture grain pouring into a cloth sack with a soft thud.
abstract.cn: 想象粮食哗啦倒进布袋的沉闷声响。

abstract.en: See a worker carrying a small bag out of the office gate.
abstract.cn: 看一名职员拎着小包走出办公室大门。

abstract.en: Watch an ancient city emptied like a turned-out bag.
abstract.cn: 看一座古城像被倒空的麻袋一样被掠走一切。

examples.en: The warehouse stores hundreds of sacks of coffee beans.
examples.cn: 仓库里储存着数百袋咖啡豆。

examples.en: She bought a sack of onions at the market.
examples.cn: 她在市场上买了一袋洋葱。

examples.en: Two workers were sacked after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后有两名工人被解雇了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞克」——把东西使劲塞进口袋里；sack 读音近似「塞克」

root: 源自希腊语 sakkos（粗布袋），经拉丁语 saccus、古法语 sac 进入英语；袋、袋量、洗劫诸义一脉相承，「解雇」义则由工人装袋离场的习语而生。

sensesIntro.en: Sack moves from a rough bag, to the amount it holds, to dismissal by the bag one carries out, and to emptied towns.
sensesIntro.cn: sack 从粗布口袋出发，到袋中所盛之量，再到拎袋走人的解雇与被倒空的城池。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one big rough bag that swallows everything
core.cn: 核心意象：一口吞得下一切的大粗布袋

branches.en: The rough cloth bag is the base image.
branches.cn: 粗布大袋是这个词的基础画面。

branches.en: The full bag becomes the unit of trade.
branches.cn: 装满的袋子顺势成为交易计量单位。

branches.en: Carrying your things out in a bag means losing the job.
branches.cn: 把私物装袋带走，意味着丢掉了工作。

branches.en: An emptied town is a sack turned inside out.
branches.cn: 被洗劫的城池就是一只被倒空的麻袋。

branches.en: Hit the sack and get the sack both end with the bag.
branches.cn: hit the sack 与 get the sack 都以那只袋子收场。

intro.en: Sack builds compounds around bags, games, and slang.
intro.cn: sack 的构词围绕口袋、游戏与俚语展开。

latinIntro.en: Sack comes from Greek through Latin, so it has classical-rooted relatives.
latinIntro.cn: sack 经拉丁语来自希腊语，故有古典词根的近亲。

items.example: The floor was covered with sacking.
He brought a sackful of apples.

items.meaning: a packed meal carried in a paper bag
items.example: She took a sack lunch on the hike.
items.exampleCN: 她带着袋装午餐去远足。

items.meaning: a game of hopping inside a sack
items.example: The sack race made everyone laugh.
items.exampleCN: 麻袋赛跑逗得大家哈哈大笑。

items.meaning: to be dismissed from a job
items.example: He got the sack for sleeping at work.
items.exampleCN: 他因上班睡觉被炒了鱿鱼。

items.example: I am tired; time to hit the sack.
Heave that sack of potatoes onto the cart.
The old banker gripped his money sack.
Each camper carried a sleeping sack.
items.exampleCN: 每位露营者都带着简易睡袋。

items.example: The sacked workers held a protest.
items.exampleCN: 被解雇的工人举行了抗议。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 粗布袋（sack 的直接来源）

definition_zh: 技术的；专业的；技术性的
definition_en: relating to machines or applied science, or using the special terms of a field
core_image: 厚厚的说明书上满是术语与示意图
scene: 说明书里全是技术术语，他读得很慢。 The manual is full of technical terms, so he reads it slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 technical 是「技术的、专业术语的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：说明书里全是技术术语，他读得很慢。

derivatives.zh: 技术上；严格说来
技术员
技巧

senses.title: Relating to machines and applied science
senses.definition: connected with machines, engineering, or applied science
senses.definitionCN: 与机器、工程或应用科学有关的
senses.example: The lab needs better technical equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室需要更好的技术设备。
senses.why: The Greek root named a craft or skill, and machines are modern crafts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根指技艺、手艺，机器是现代的手艺。

senses.title: Using special terms
senses.definition: using the special words of a particular field
senses.definitionCN: 使用某一领域专门用语的
senses.example: The manual is full of technical terms.
senses.exampleCN: 说明书里全是专业术语。
senses.why: Every craft has its own words, so its language is technical.
senses.whyCN: 每门手艺都有自己的说法，因此这种语言就是「专业的」。

senses.title: Following strict rules
senses.definition: judged by the exact rules of a sport or system
senses.definitionCN: 按运动或制度的严格规则判定的
senses.example: The player was given a technical foul.
senses.exampleCN: 这名球员被判技术犯规。
senses.why: A rule applied exactly is a technical judgment.
senses.whyCN: 严格照规则执行，就是技术性判定。

intro.en: Technical comes from the Greek word for craft and skill.
intro.cn: technical 来自希腊语中表示技艺与手艺的词。

items.en: Techne meant art, craft, and skill.
items.cn: techne 意为技艺、手艺与技能。

items.en: Technicus described a skilled craftsman.
items.cn: technicus 形容有手艺的工匠。

items.en: Technical entered English for matters of art and craft.
items.cn: technical 先指技艺与工艺之事。

items.en: It shifted toward machines and engineering.
items.cn: 它转向机器与工程。

items.en: It also means specialized and rule-bound.
items.cn: 它也表示专业术语与严格按规则。

note.en: Technical is compared with look-alike forms and with words for skilled work.
note.cn: 把 technical 与形近形式以及表示技艺的词作对比。

entries.definition: in a technical way
entries.definitionCN: 技术上

entries.definition: a skilled worker
entries.definitionCN: 技术员

entries.definition: a way of doing something
entries.definitionCN: 技巧

entries.definition: about machines
entries.definitionCN: 机械的

entries.definition: focused on one field
entries.definitionCN: 专门的

entries.definition: useful in real situations
entries.definitionCN: 实用的

normalIntro.en: Technical points to the craft behind a machine or a rule.
normalIntro.cn: technical 指向机器或规则背后的那门手艺。

normal.en: The manual is full of technical terms.
normal.cn: 说明书里全是专业术语。

normal.en: Call technical support if it fails.
normal.cn: 出故障就打技术支持电话。

normal.en: He studied at a technical college.
normal.cn: 他在技术学院读书。

normal.en: The delay was a technical problem.
normal.cn: 延误是技术故障造成的。

normal.en: The referee called a technical foul.
normal.cn: 裁判判了技术犯规。

abstract.en: Every machine is a craft that learned to move.
abstract.cn: 每台机器都是学会移动的手艺。

abstract.en: Special words guard a special skill.
abstract.cn: 专门的词守护专门的技能。

abstract.en: Rules applied exactly become technical.
abstract.cn: 规则被精确执行就成了技术性判定。

examples.en: The manual is full of technical terms, so he reads it slowly.
examples.cn: 说明书里全是技术术语，他读得很慢。

examples.en: The lab needs better technical equipment.
examples.cn: 实验室需要更好的技术设备。

examples.en: The player was given a technical foul.
examples.cn: 这名球员被判技术犯规。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太克你」——机器技术太难，「太克」住你了，就是技术性的难题。

root: 希腊语 techne（技艺、手艺）经拉丁语 technicus 进入英语，核心是「与手艺有关」。

sensesIntro.en: Technical moves from craft, to machines, to the special language of a field, to strict rule judgments.
sensesIntro.cn: technical 从手艺，到机器，到某领域的专门语言，再到按规则作出的判定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a manual dense with diagrams and small print.
core.cn: 核心意象：满是示意图与小字的说明书。

branches.en: Machines are modern craft.
branches.cn: 机器是现代手艺。

branches.en: Each craft has its own words.

branches.en: Rules applied exactly look technical.

branches.en: Equipment and its vocabulary travel together.
branches.cn: 设备与它的词汇同行。

branches.en: Both appeal to exact standards.

intro.cn: technical 撑起 technique、technician、technology 一大族词。

latinIntro.en: Greek techne, craft, passed into Latin as technicus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 techne（技艺）以 technicus 进入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 地区的；区域的；地区性的；地方（性）的
definition_en: relating to a particular region of a country or the world, or existing only in one region
core_image: 地图上被圈出来的一大块土地：圈里的事在圈里发生，圈外各有各的圈
scene: 周末市集上，北边山城带来的苹果总要早熟半个月，风味也不同。 Regional differences in climate shape the fruit harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 regional 是「地区的；区域性的」（第 1 个义项：属于某一地区的）；句意：各区域的气候差异塑造了果实的收成。场景要点：摊位上的苹果、地图与价牌。

pos.zh: 地区的；区域的；地区性的；局部的

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「地区；区域；范围」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「地方主义；地区特征；区域主义」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「在地区层面；按地区」
由形容词加动词后缀构成，义为「使按地区划分；使地区化」

senses.title: Of or typical of a region
senses.definition: relating to, or characteristic of, one particular large area of a country or continent
senses.definitionCN: 与某个国家或大陆的一大块地区相关，或为其所特有
senses.example: Regional dialects fade fastest in the big coastal cities.
senses.exampleCN: 地区方言在沿海大城市消失得最快。
senses.why: The word simply adds the idea of the drawn boundary: everything inside the circle is regional.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是加上「画出的边界」之意：圈内的万物都是 regional 的。

senses.title: Limited to one region
senses.definition: existing, operating, or available only within one region and not nationally or globally
senses.definitionCN: 只在一个区域内存续、运营或可用，而非全国或全球性的
senses.example: It is a regional bank with branches in three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一家区域性银行，在三个省设有分行。
senses.why: The circle now works as a limit: what happens inside does not cross the line.
senses.whyCN: 此时这个圈起的是限制作用：圈内之事不越界。

senses.title: Run by or serving a region
senses.definition: of an organization, office, or facility, operated at the level of a region rather than centrally or locally
senses.definitionCN: 指机构、办公室或设施按地区层级运作，而非中央或基层层面
senses.example: She moved to the firm's regional office in Chengdu.
senses.exampleCN: 她调到了公司在成都的地区办公室。
senses.why: Between the whole country and the single town lies the middle circle: regional is the layer drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 在整国与小镇之间有个中间圈：regional 就是画在两者之间的那一层。

senses.title: Local in a medical sense
senses.definition: affecting or limited to one part or area of the body, as in regional anaesthesia
senses.definitionCN: 影响或局限于身体某个部位，如 regional anaesthesia
senses.example: The surgeon chose regional anaesthesia instead of a general one.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生选择了局部麻醉而非全身麻醉。
senses.why: The map metaphor shrinks to the body: one district of the flesh is numbed while the rest stays awake.
senses.whyCN: 地图比喻缩到身体上：肉身的一个「辖区」被麻醉，其余保持清醒。

intro.en: Regional is the adjective of region, from Latin regio 'direction, boundary, district', from regere 'to keep straight, rule'. A region was first a line drawn straight across the land; the adjective keeps the drawn line in every use.
intro.cn: regional 是 region 的形容词，region 出自拉丁语 regio「方向、边界、地区」，上溯 regere「保持笔直、统治」。region 起初是画在大地上的一条直线；形容词在每种用法里都保留这条画线。

items.en: The root *h3reg- 'to straighten, direct' underlies both regere and its noun family; right, rule and rich are distant English cousins.
items.cn: 词根 *h3reg-「拉直、引导」同时生出 regere 及其名词家族；right、rule、rich 是英语中的远亲。

items.en: Regio meant 'a direction of the sky or land, a boundary, a district': first the straight line, then the territory it marks off.
items.cn: regio 意为「天或地的一个方向、边界、地区」：先是那条直线，再是直线圈出的地盘。

items.en: Region passes through Old French rejon into English in the thirteenth century with the sense 'land under one rule, district'.
items.cn: region 经古法语 rejon 于十三世纪进入英语，意为「同一统治下的土地、地区」。

items.en: The adjective regional forms in English in the seventeenth century, at first rare, marking things that belong to a district.
items.cn: 形容词 regional 于十七世纪在英语中成形，起初罕见，标记「属于某一地区之物」。

items.en: Modern administration spreads the word: regional governments, railways and headquarters make the middle layer of organisation official.
items.cn: 现代行政使这个词普及：地区政府、铁路与总部让「中间层级」的组织获得了正式名分。

note.en: The first group gathers the regere 'draw the line' family around the district word. The second group compares the adjectives of place, from the street to the globe.
note.cn: 第一组汇集围绕「地区」一词的 regere「画线」词族。第二组比较从街巷到全球的「地点」形容词。

entries.definition: a large area of land marked off by nature or administration. It is the word regional circles.
entries.definitionCN: 由自然或行政划出的大片陆地。regional 所圈画的正是它。

entries.definition: loyalty to one's own region, or a local word and custom. The circle turns into a flag.
entries.definitionCN: 对本地区的忠诚，或地方性词语与风俗。圈变成了旗。

entries.definition: following a rule or even spacing. It keeps the straight bar of regula rather than the drawn district.
entries.definitionCN: 守规则的、间隔均匀的。它保留 regula 的直杆，而非画出的地区。

entries.definition: to control by rule. The straightening hand again, applied to systems.
entries.definitionCN: 用规则管制。又是那只引直之手，这次用在体系上。

entries.definition: a system of ruling. The district is what is ruled; the regime is the ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 统治体系。地区是被治之物，regime 是治理本身。

entries.definition: belonging to a small place, a town or neighbourhood. Local is the smaller circle inside the regional one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于小镇或街区这样的小地方。local 是 regional 里面更小的圈。

entries.definition: of a province, sometimes with a tinge of narrow-mindedness. Provincial draws its line by province.
entries.definitionCN: 省的，有时略带见识短浅之意。provincial 以省画线。

entries.definition: covering the whole country. National is the biggest circle of the same set.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖全国的。national 是同套圆圈里最大的一个。

entries.definition: of a territory or claiming one. It stresses ownership and defence of the marked land.
entries.definitionCN: 领土的；主张领地的。它强调对画线土地的拥有与防卫。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regere 'to rule, keep straight' behind region, regime, regular and regulate, and the picture of a boundary drawn on the map.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regere「统治、保持笔直」生出 region、regime、regular、regulate，以及地图上画出的边界图景。

normal.en: Region comes from regere: the ruler's straight line across the land becomes the district.
normal.cn: region 出自 regere：统治者画过大地的那条直线变成了地区。

normal.en: The suffix -al simply means 'of': regional is 'of the region'.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 只表示「属于」：regional 就是「属于地区的」。

normal.en: Regional, national and local are three circles of the same map.
normal.cn: regional、national、local 是同一张地图上的三个圆圈。

normal.en: Regionalism adds -ism: the circle you were born inside becomes a loyalty.
normal.cn: regionalism 加上 -ism：你出生的那个圈变成一种忠诚。

normal.en: In medicine the circle shrinks: regional anaesthesia numbs only one district of the body.
normal.cn: 在医学里圆圈缩小：局部麻醉只麻木身体的一个「辖区」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand drawing one straight line across a folded map: everything on one side of it shares a fate.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在摊开的地图上画一条直线：线同一侧的一切共享同一种命运。

abstract.en: Every region is a rule made visible: the line you can see is the rule you live inside.
abstract.cn: 每个地区都是一条可见的规则：你看得见的线，就是你生活于其中的规则。

abstract.en: Regional news is what matters inside the circle and nowhere else.
abstract.cn: 地区新闻就是只在这个圈内重要、别处无关的事。

examples.en: The supermarket chain adjusts its stock to regional tastes.
examples.cn: 这家连锁超市根据地区口味调整货品。

examples.en: Regional trains stop at every small town along the valley.
examples.cn: 地区列车在山谷沿线每个小镇都停靠。

examples.en: The regional finals were held in Hangzhou this year.
examples.cn: 今年的区域决赛在杭州举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞吉恩闹」——瑞福在地图上把「区域」用线一「圈」就「闹」明白了 → regional 地区的；区域的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regio「地区、边界」（regere 引直、统治），核心是「被一条线圈出的土地」，形容词只是给这块地加上「属于」的标签。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of regional, all one circle seen four ways: the district itself, the limit it sets, the layer of management it creates, and the small circle drawn on the body.
sensesIntro.cn: regional 的四个义项是同一个圆圈的四种看法：地区本身、它划定的限制、它形成的管理层级，以及画在身体上的小圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn across the land, marking off a district.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条画过大地的直线，圈出一块地区。

chain: SHRINK THE CIRCLE TO THE BODY

branches.en: THE DISTRICT: character and products that belong inside the drawn line.
branches.cn: 地区：属于线内之地的风物与特产。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: banks, dialects and media that stop at the boundary.
branches.cn: 限制：止步于边界的银行、方言与媒体。

branches.en: THE LAYER: offices and services run at the level between town and nation.
branches.cn: 层级：介于城镇与国家之间的办公室与服务。

branches.en: THE BODY: the drawn line becomes the surgeon's outline around one part of the flesh.
branches.cn: 身体：画线变成外科医生围住身体一部分的轮廓。

branches.en: TWO FACES OF ONE CIRCLE: what the line holds together is also what the line holds apart.
branches.cn: 一个圆的两面：线聚拢起来的，也正是线隔开来的。

intro.en: Regional adds the Latin adjective suffix -al to region, the district noun of regere 'to keep straight, rule'. The regere family also gives regular, regulate, regime and regionalism.
intro.cn: regional 在 region——regere「保持笔直、统治」的「地区」名词——上添加拉丁形容词后缀 -al。regere 词族还给出 regular、regulate、regime、regionalism。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regio 'boundary, direction, district', from regere 'to draw straight, rule'. The line that rules the land becomes the land between the lines.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regio「边界、方向、地区」，出自 regere「画直、统治」。治理大地的线，变成了线与线之间的土地。

items.meaning: of a region; limited to a region
items.meaningCN: 地区的；区域的（-al 表示「属于」）
items.example: Regional airports link the smaller cities.
items.exampleCN: 区域性机场连接较小的城市。

items.meaning: a large area marked off by nature or rule
items.meaningCN: 地区；区域（-io 构成名词）
items.example: The region is famous for its tea.

items.meaning: loyalty to one's region; a local feature
items.meaningCN: 地方主义；地区特征（-ism 表示倾向）
items.example: The novel is full of regionalism in its dialogue.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说的对话充满地方色彩。

items.meaning: at the level of a region
items.meaningCN: 在地区层面（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The prizes are judged regionally first.

items.meaningCN: 使按地区划分（-ize 表示「使成为」）
items.example: The company regionalized its sales teams.
items.exampleCN: 公司把销售团队按地区重组了。

items.meaning: following a rule; even in spacing
items.meaningCN: 规律的；规则的（-ar 构成形容词）
items.example: Regular sleep keeps the body steady.
items.exampleCN: 规律睡眠让身体保持平稳。

items.meaningCN: 管制；调节（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: Rules regulate the use of parkland.
items.exampleCN: 规则管制着公园用地的使用。

items.meaning: a system of rule; a planned routine
items.meaningCN: 政权；体制；方案（-men 构成结果名词）
items.example: The training regime lasts six weeks.

items.meaning: between nations; crossing the biggest circles
items.meaningCN: 国际的（inter- 之间 + nation + -al，是同一套圆圈之外的更大范围）
items.example: International flights leave from Terminal Two.
items.exampleCN: 国际航班从第二航站楼出发。

items.meaningCN: 领土；属地（出自 terra「土地」，与 region 词源不同但义近）
items.example: Dogs defend their territory against strangers.
items.exampleCN: 狗会防御领地不受陌生者侵犯。

definition_zh: 行为；举止；实施；进行；指挥；传导
definition_en: the way a person behaves, or to organize an activity and carry it out
core_image: 乐队指挥举起双手，让整个乐团同时发声
scene: 老师带学生参观实验室，提醒大家注意行为举止。 His conduct in the lab impressed every teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 conduct 指「行为举止」（第 1 个义项：一个人在公开场合的表现）；句意是他在实验室里的举止让每位老师都印象深刻。

derivatives.zh: 传导；输送
导电的；导热的
传导性；导电率
指挥；导体；售票员
不当行为；失职

senses.title: The way one behaves
senses.definition: the way a person acts, especially in public or at work
senses.definitionCN: 一个人行事的方式，尤指在公开场合或工作中的表现
senses.example: His conduct during the meeting was calm.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会议上的举止很沉稳。
senses.why: Others cannot see your motives, so they judge what you do.
senses.whyCN: 别人看不见你的动机，只能凭你的所做来判断。

senses.title: Carry out an activity
senses.definition: to organize and carry out a plan, test or study
senses.definitionCN: 组织并完成计划、测试或研究
senses.example: The team conducted a survey of local farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 团队对当地农民做了一次调查。
senses.why: An activity needs someone to lead it from start to finish.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动需要有人从头到尾带着走。

senses.title: Lead a group or carry energy
senses.definition: to direct a group such as an orchestra, or to carry heat or electricity
senses.definitionCN: 指挥乐团等团体，或输送热与电
senses.example: Copper conducts electricity very well.
senses.exampleCN: 铜的导电性非常好。
senses.why: A leader and a wire both carry something from one end to the other.
senses.whyCN: 领导者与电线都在把某样东西从一端送到另一端。

intro.en: Conduct comes from Latin conducere, to lead together, built from com-, together, and ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: conduct 来自拉丁语 conducere，意为一起带领，由 com-（一起）与 ducere（引导）构成。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead a person or an army along a road.
items.cn: ducere 意为带着人或军队沿路前行。

items.en: Conducere meant to bring several things together under one lead.
items.cn: conducere 意为把几件事物收拢到同一个带领之下。

items.en: Old French conduire used the word for guiding and managing.
items.cn: 古法语 conduire 用这个词表示引导与管理。

items.en: English conduct first named the act of leading or guiding.
items.cn: 英语 conduct 最初指带领与引导的行为。

items.en: It now covers behaviour as well as the carrying of heat and electricity.
items.cn: 如今它既指行为举止，也指热与电的输送。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same Latin lead base, and the meaning group names other ways of behaving or leading.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在同一拉丁词基上的词，近义组列出其他表示行为或带领的说法。

entries.definition: a pipe or channel that carries something
entries.definitionCN: 管道；通道

entries.definition: helping to make a result likely
entries.definitionCN: 有助于…的

entries.definition: to take an amount away from a total
entries.definitionCN: 扣除；减去

entries.definition: the way a person or animal acts
entries.definitionCN: 行为；举止

entries.definition: to move something from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 携带；传送

entries.definition: to control the way an activity is done
entries.definitionCN: 指挥；指导

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a conductor raising a baton, then move to a research team and to a copper wire.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从举起指挥棒的人开始，再走到研究团队与一根铜线。

normal.en: Con- is together and duct- is lead, so conduct is to lead things together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，duct- 是引导，所以 conduct 就是把事情一起带着走。

normal.en: A teacher conducts a class, and a wire conducts a current.
normal.cn: 老师带领一个班级，电线传导一股电流。

normal.en: Your conduct is simply how you lead yourself in public.
normal.cn: 你的行为举止，就是你在人前带领自己的方式。

normal.en: To conduct a survey, first write down what you want to ask.
normal.cn: 要开展调查，先写下你想问的内容。

normal.en: Bad conduct at work can end a career faster than bad luck.
normal.cn: 工作中的不当行为，比运气不好更快毁掉前程。

abstract.en: Picture a baton drawing one line through the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指挥棒在空中划出一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow pipe carrying water downhill.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细管把水引向低处。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd following one person through a gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人跟着一个人穿过大门。

examples.en: The school expects good conduct from every student.
examples.cn: 学校要求每位学生行为端正。

examples.en: They conducted the experiment twice to be sure.
examples.cn: 他们把这个实验做了两次以求稳妥。

examples.en: This metal conducts heat better than iron.
examples.cn: 这种金属比铁的导热性更好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conduct 记成 con（一起）加 duct（引导）：把一群人一起带着走，是指挥与实施；把自己带着走，就是行为举止。

root: 源自拉丁语 conducere（com 一起 + ducere 引导），本义是一起带领，后引申为实施、指挥、传导与行为举止。

sensesIntro.en: From leading a group, to carrying out a study, and finally to the way one carries oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从带领一群人，到开展一项研究，最后到一个人立身行事的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one raised hand leads an orchestra, a team, or a current of electricity.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手，带着乐团、团队或一股电流。

branches.en: Conduct as behaviour is the self under the eyes of others.
branches.cn: 行为义项是自我在别人目光下的样子。

branches.en: To conduct a study is to lead it from question to answer.
branches.cn: 开展研究就是从问题一直领到答案。

branches.en: Leading a group and carrying a current share the same movement.
branches.cn: 带领团队与传导电流共享同一种运动。

branches.en: Good conduct helps any activity run smoothly.
branches.cn: 良好的举止能让任何活动顺利开展。

branches.en: Both senses need a clear path from one end to the other.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要一条从一端到另一端的畅通路径。

intro.en: Conduct is built on Latin com-, together, plus ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: conduct 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 ducere（引导）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin lead base duct- also appears in product, reduce and introduce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的引导词基 duct- 也出现在 product、reduce 与 introduce 中。

items.example: They conducted the test in silence.
items.exampleCN: 他们在安静中完成了测试。

items.meaning: the passing of heat or electricity
items.example: Conduction carries heat along the bar.
items.exampleCN: 传导把热量沿着金属棒送过去。

items.meaning: able to carry heat or electricity
items.example: Silver is a highly conductive metal.
items.exampleCN: 银是导电性很强的金属。

items.meaning: a person who leads or a material that carries

items.example: The officer was dismissed for misconduct.
items.exampleCN: 这名官员因失职被免职。

definition_zh: 实际的；真实的；现实的；现有的；事实上的
definition_en: real and existing in fact, rather than imagined, claimed or expected
core_image: 手按在实物上：不是图样，不是说法，就是眼前这一件
scene: 图纸上的数字很好看，可工人到现场一量，尺寸差了两指。 The actual cost was almost twice the estimate.
sceneCN: 这里 actual 指「真实发生的数额」（第 2 个义项：与声称或估算相对的实际数额）；句意为实际成本几乎是估算的两倍。

pos.zh: 形容词：实际的；真实的；现有的；事实上的
名词（常用复数）：实际数字；实际发生的数据

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；竟然」
由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「现实；实际情况」
由本词加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「实现；使成为现实」
由动词 actualize 加名词后缀构成，义为「实现；现实化」

senses.title: Real, not imagined or invented
senses.definition: existing in fact and not produced by imagination, rumour or invention
senses.definitionCN: 真实存在的，而非想象、传言或编造出来的
senses.example: The film is based on the actual events of that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片依据那个冬天的真实事件改编。
senses.why: Latin actualis meant 'active, practical'; from 'what is done' the sense slid to 'what really is', because a deed leaves something behind that others can check.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 actualis 本义是「行动的、实际的」；从「被做出来的事」滑向「真实存在的东西」，因为行为会留下别人能核对的痕迹。

senses.title: The real amount behind a claim
senses.titleCN: 与声称或估算相对的实际数额
senses.definition: used of a sum, cost or figure to mean the one that truly applies, as opposed to an estimate or a claim
senses.definitionCN: 用于金额、成本或数字，指真正适用的那一个，与估算或声称相对
senses.example: The actual cost was almost twice the estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 实际成本几乎是估算的两倍。
senses.why: When a number is announced, people ask what was really done; the adjective marks the measured figure against the spoken one.
senses.whyCN: 数字被报出来时，人们会问真正做了多少；这个形容词就把量出来的数与被说出来的数区分开。

senses.title: Exact and precise
senses.definition: used to stress that a figure or word is the exact one, not an approximate one
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调某个数字或词语是确切的那一个，而非约略的说法
senses.example: Do you know the actual number of people who came?
senses.exampleCN: 你知道来的人的确切数目吗？
senses.why: If actual picks out what truly is, then in talk about numbers it picks out the precise value rather than a round one.
senses.whyCN: 如果 actual 挑出的是「真正存在的」，那么在谈数字时，它挑出的就是精确值而不是约数。

senses.title: Existing at the present time
senses.definition: used of a situation or state to mean the one that exists now, as opposed to a past or future one
senses.definitionCN: 用于情况或状态，指当下存在的那个，与过去或未来相对
senses.example: We need to describe the actual situation, not the one we hope for.
senses.exampleCN: 我们要描述的是现有情况，而不是我们希望出现的情况。
senses.why: What is real is real now; the adjective therefore slides from 'real' to 'current' whenever a situation is being compared across time.
senses.whyCN: 真实的东西是在此刻真实的；所以只要把情况放在时间上比较，这个词就从「真实」滑向「当前」。

senses.title: Practical rather than theoretical
senses.titleCN: 实际操作中的（与理论相对）
senses.definition: used of results or conditions in real use, as opposed to what theory or a design predicts
senses.definitionCN: 指真实使用中的结果或条件，与理论或设计的预测相对
senses.example: The actual performance of the engine was far below the brochure.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机的实际表现远低于宣传册上的数字。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word: actualis named what is done in practice, and theory is what has not yet been done.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层：actualis 指在实践中做出来的东西，而理论是尚未做出来的东西。

senses.title: In effect, whether lawful or not
senses.definition: used of power or control that is really exercised, whether or not it is officially recognised
senses.definitionCN: 指真正被行使的权力或控制，无论是否得到正式承认
senses.example: The general held actual control of the region for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位将军多年来掌握着该地区的实际控制权。
senses.why: Law distinguishes the paper title from the hand that holds the key, and actual marks the hand.
senses.whyCN: 法律要把纸面上的名分和真正拿着钥匙的那只手分开，actual 标的就是那只手。

senses.title: Legal: actual rather than presumed
senses.titleCN: 法律上的「实际的」（与推定相对）
senses.definition: in law, describing knowledge, notice or authority that is proved to exist, as opposed to one the law presumes
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中形容经证明存在的知情、通知或授权，与法律推定相对
senses.example: The court found actual notice, not merely constructive notice.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定存在实际知悉，而不仅仅是推定知悉。
senses.why: Legal systems already have a word for what is presumed; they need the opposite term for what can be shown, and actual fills that slot.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系本来就有词表示「推定」，还需要一个相反的词表示「能举证证实的」，actual 正好补上这个位置。

senses.title: Actuals: recorded figures in finance
senses.definition: as a plural noun in accounting, the figures that have really been earned or spent, compared with a budget or forecast
senses.definitionCN: 会计中作复数名词，指真实发生收入或支出的数字，用以与预算或预测比较
senses.example: The report compares this year's actuals with the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把今年的实际数据与预算作了比较。
senses.why: Once 'actual' is fixed as the opposite of forecast, it can stand alone as a noun: the actuals are the numbers that really happened.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 actual 被固定为 forecast 的对立面，它就能单独作名词：actuals 就是真正发生了的那些数字。

intro.en: Actual comes from the same Latin root as act, but it entered English meaning 'active' and only later shifted to 'real'.
intro.cn: actual 与 act 同出拉丁词根，但它进入英语时意思是「活跃的」，后来才转为「真实的」。

items.en: *ag- is generally reconstructed as 'to drive, set in motion'; the deeper origin of this root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ag- 表示「驱动、使运动」；这个词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Agere meant 'to drive, do, act', and its past participle actus gave the noun for a deed.
items.cn: agere 意为「驱动、做、行动」，其过去分词 actus 给出了表示「行为」的名词。

items.en: Late Latin actualis meant 'active, practical, of a deed', formed from actus plus the adjective suffix -alis.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 actualis 意为「活跃的、实际的、与行为有关的」，由 actus 加形容词后缀 -alis 构成。

items.en: English borrowed the word through Old French actuel, where it still meant 'active, practical' rather than 'real'.
items.cn: 英语经古法语 actuel 借入这个词，当时它仍表示「活跃的、实际的」，而非「真实的」。

items.en: The modern sense 'existing in fact' established itself in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and the old sense 'active' survives mainly in actuality and in the adverb.
items.cn: 「真实存在的」这一现代义在十六、十七世纪确立；旧的「活跃」义主要残留在 actuality 与副词形式里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the act family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is real, each with a different test of reality.
note.cn: 形近组收 act 词族；近义组收表示「真实」的词，各自检验真实的标准不同。

entries.definition: The noun for reality or for real circumstances, formed with -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「现实、实际情况」，由本词加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: To make something real, formed with the verb suffix -ize.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现、使成为现实」，由本词加动词后缀构成。

entries.definition: The base verb and noun meaning to do something or a thing done.
entries.definitionCN: 动词兼名词，义为「行动、行为」，是本词的基础词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning busy or taking part; it keeps the older sense of actual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活跃的、积极参与的」，保留了 actual 较早的那层含义。

entries.definition: Existing as a thing rather than as an idea; the broadest and plainest of these words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「真实的、实在的」，是这组词里范围最宽也最朴素的一个。

entries.definition: Real and not faked; the test is authenticity rather than existence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「真正的、非伪造的」，检验的是真伪而非是否存在。

entries.definition: Based on facts and able to be checked; it describes accounts rather than things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基于事实的」，描述的是叙述而非事物本身。

entries.definition: Specific and definite, the opposite of vague; it tests precision of detail.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「具体的、明确的」，与含糊相对，检验的是细节是否确定。

entries.definition: In accordance with the facts; used of statements, not of costs or objects.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正确的、符合事实的」，多用于陈述，而非成本或物件。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin suffix, the shift from 'active' to 'real', and the phrases that keep the word alive.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借助拉丁后缀、从「活跃」到「真实」的语义转变，以及让这个词活着的常见搭配。

normal.en: Actus is a deed, and -alis means 'of'; actual at first meant 'of a deed', that is, practical.
normal.cn: actus 是「行为」，-alis 表示「与……有关」；actual 最初就是「与行为有关的」，也就是实际的。

normal.en: In actual fact keeps the old and the new sense side by side.
normal.cn: in actual fact 这个搭配把新旧两层意思并排放着。

normal.en: The actual cost is what the bill says, not what the estimate said.
normal.cn: the actual cost 是账单上写的数，不是估算时说的数。

normal.en: Add -ly and you get the adverb actually, which lives a very different life.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly 就得到副词 actually，它的用法完全是另一套。

normal.en: In law, actual notice is proved, while constructive notice is presumed.
normal.cn: 在法律里，actual notice 是被证明的，constructive notice 是被推定的。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed flat on a table: the table is there whether or not anyone describes it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平按在桌面上：无论有没有人描述，桌子都在那里。

abstract.en: A drawing of the table can be wrong; the table that the hand touches cannot.
abstract.cn: 桌子的图可能画错；手摸到的那张桌子不会错。

abstract.en: Every sense of actual is a test of that touch: does it exist, is it exact, is it now, does it hold power.
abstract.cn: actual 的每个义项都是对这一次触摸的检验：它存在吗、精确吗、是现在吗、握着权力吗。

examples.en: The actual cost was almost twice the estimate.
examples.cn: 实际成本几乎是估算的两倍。

examples.en: Do you know the actual number of people who came?
examples.cn: 你知道来的人的确切数目吗？

examples.en: The report compares this year's actuals with the budget.
examples.cn: 这份报告把今年的实际数据与预算作了比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克图」——图上画的不算，手上摸到的才作数：实际的、真实的。

root: 拉丁语 actualis「活跃的、实际的」由 actus「行为」加形容词后缀 -alis 构成，而 actus 出自 agere「驱动、做」的过去分词；英语经古法语 actuel 借入。

sensesIntro.en: One adjective keeps asking what is really there: a real event, a measured sum, an exact figure, the present state, practical results, power in hand, proved knowledge, or the numbers in a ledger.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个形容词一直在追问「真正在那里的是什么」：真实的事件、量出来的金额、确切的数字、当下的状态、实践中的结果、手中的权力、被证明的知情，或账本上的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat hand on a solid object, checking that it is really there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌按在实物上，确认它真的在那里。

branches.en: THE THING ITSELF: what happened is not what was imagined or invented.
branches.cn: 事物本身线：发生过的事，不是想象或编造出来的。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: the measured figure beats the spoken or estimated one, and the exact value beats the round one.
branches.cn: 数字线：量出来的数胜过说出来的数和估算，精确值胜过约数。

branches.en: THE PRESENT AND THE PRACTICE: what is real is real now, and real results are the ones seen in use.
branches.cn: 当下与实践线：真实的东西在此刻真实，真实的结果是在使用中看到的结果。

branches.en: THE LAW: actual marks the power that is truly held and the knowledge that can be proved.
branches.cn: 法律线：actual 标出真正握有的权力和能够被证明的知情。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: once set against forecast, the word can stand alone as a plural noun.
branches.cn: 账本线：一旦与预测相对，这个词就能单独作复数名词使用。

intro.en: Actual is the Latin adjective of the act root; English then adds -ly, -ity and -ize to build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: actual 是 act 词根的拉丁形容词形式；英语再通过 -ly、-ity 与 -ize 长出其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Agere, actus and actualis are recorded Latin forms; the Indo-European root above them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: agere、actus 与 actualis 都是有文献记录的拉丁语形式；更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The root lies behind Latin agere.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根藏在拉丁语 agere 之后。

items.example: Agere is the ultimate source of the family.
items.exampleCN: agere 是这一词族的最初来源。

items.example: Actus is the noun that actualis was built on.
items.exampleCN: actus 正是构成 actualis 的那个名词。

items.example: Actualis is the direct source of actual.
items.exampleCN: actualis 是 actual 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 调皮的；不听话的；下流的
definition_en: badly behaved, especially of a child; or containing rude or sexual jokes and words
core_image: 一个藏在沙发后偷吃饼干、被逮个正着的小孩
scene: 客厅里，大人转身拿茶的工夫，沙发后面探出一个沾满饼干渣的小脑袋。 The naughty boy had taken all the biscuits again.
sceneCN: 这里 naughty 是「调皮的、不听话的」（第 1 个义项：孩子淘气、违反规矩）；句意为这个调皮的男孩又把饼干全拿走了。图中可辨识物件：沙发、饼干渣、茶杯。

pos.zh: 调皮的；不听话的；下流的

derivatives.zh: 由 naughty 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「调皮地；不听话地」
由 naughty 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「淘气；顽皮」

senses.title: Badly behaved, especially of a child
senses.definition: used of a child or pet that does not do what it is told and breaks rules in a mild way
senses.definitionCN: 用于孩子或宠物，指不听大人的话、轻微违反规矩
senses.example: The naughty puppy hid my slippers under the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 这只调皮的小狗把我的拖鞋藏到了床底下。
senses.why: The word grew out of naught, meaning nothing or no good, so a naughty child is one whose behaviour falls short of what is good.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 naught（无、没什么好）长出来，所以 naughty 的孩子就是行为「不及于善」、不够听话的孩子。

senses.title: Mildly disobedient in a playful way
senses.titleCN: 顽皮的；带点恶作剧意味的
senses.definition: used of playful rule-breaking that is charming rather than truly bad, as in an extra dessert or a skipped chore
senses.definitionCN: 用于带乐趣的小小违规，比如多吃一份甜品或偷懒不做家务，并非真正恶劣
senses.example: She had a second slice of cake and said it was very naughty of her.
senses.exampleCN: 她多吃了第二块蛋糕，说自己真是太不乖了。
senses.why: Because the blame in naughty is mild and affectionate, adults borrow it for small guilty pleasures that break no real rules.
senses.whyCN: naughty 带的责备很轻、还带疼爱，于是大人也借它来形容无伤大雅的小小放纵。

senses.title: Rude or sexual in language or humour
senses.definition: used of jokes, words or pictures that deal with sex in a way polite talk avoids
senses.definitionCN: 用于笑话、词语或图片，指以礼貌言语避谈的方式涉及性
senses.example: The comedian told a few naughty jokes at the end of the show.
senses.exampleCN: 喜剧演员在演出快结束时讲了几个下流的笑话。
senses.why: Adult speech stretches the child's small sin into the grown-up one: what is not said in public is naughty, so the word slides to rude humour.
senses.whyCN: 小孩的小小出格被放大为成年人的出格：不宜公开说出口的话就是 naughty，词义于是滑向下流幽默。

intro.en: The word is built on the old English noun naught, meaning nothing or evil, with the adjective ending -y, so its history is plain and well recorded.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在古英语名词 naught（意为「无、恶」）之上，加形容词词尾 -y 构成，源流清楚、记录完整。

items.en: The root behind naught is a reconstructed Germanic compound of not and aught, giving the sense of no thing at all.
items.cn: naught 的词根一般重构为日耳曼语的复合形式，由 not 与 aught 合成，意为「什么都没有」。

items.en: Forms such as nawt and nawiht meant nothing, and by extension also evil or wickedness.
items.cn: 古英语里 nawt、nawiht 等形式意为「无」，引申也指「恶、坏事」。

items.en: Naught keeps both senses: nothing, and moral badness, which prepares the ground for the adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语里 naught 同时保有「无」与「恶」两义，为形容词的诞生做好了铺垫。

items.en: Naughty is first recorded in the fourteenth century, meaning having naught, that is, good for nothing or wicked.
items.cn: 十四世纪首次记录 naughty，意为「一无所有」，即毫无价值、品行恶劣。

items.en: The severe sense of morally bad softens, and the word settles on children and pets that disobey.
items.cn: 「品行恶劣」的严厉义逐渐软化，这个词固定下来专指不听话的孩子和宠物。

items.en: Modern English keeps the mild sense for children and adds the adult sense of rude or sexual humour.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了针对孩子的轻微义，又添了指粗俗、涉性幽默的成人用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the word family built on naught; the near-meaning group collects words for misbehaviour and rude humour.
note.cn: 形近组收以 naught 为核心的词族；近义组收表示不听话与粗俗幽默的词。

entries.definition: An old word for nothing or zero, the noun that naughty is built on.
entries.definitionCN: naughty 所从出的名词，古旧用法，意为「无；零」。

entries.definition: The adverb made from naughty with -ly, meaning in a naughty way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 naughty 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「调皮地；不听话地」。

entries.definition: The noun made from naughty with -ness, meaning the quality of being naughty.
entries.definitionCN: 由 naughty 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「淘气；顽皮」。

entries.definition: Playfully causing trouble, especially of children who enjoy small pranks.
entries.definitionCN: 顽皮的；爱恶作剧的，尤指以小捣蛋为乐的孩子。

entries.definition: Refusing to obey rules or the people in charge, a more formal word than naughty.
entries.definitionCN: 不服从的；违抗的，比 naughty 更正式、责备更重。

entries.definition: Impolite or offensive, covering the adult sense of naughty jokes and words.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁的；冒犯的，涵盖 naughty 表示下流玩笑的成人用法。

normalIntro.en: The family is small and grows straight out of the old noun naught, so the history itself is the best memory hook.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族很小，直接从古名词 naught 长出，词史本身就是最好的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Naughty begins with naught, nothing, so a naughty child is one who does no good at that moment.
normal.cn: naughty 开头就是 naught（无），所以 naughty 的孩子就是那一刻「没干好事」的孩子。

normal.en: Naught and aught are a pair: naught means nothing and aught means anything, and naughty keeps the negative side.
normal.cn: naught 与 aught 成对：前者是「无」，后者是「有」，naughty 继承的是否定的一边。

normal.en: Naughtily and naughtiness are plain suffix jobs, so the family is easy to keep straight.
normal.cn: naughtily 与 naughtiness 都只是普通后缀加工，词族一目了然。

normal.en: Parents say naughty but rarely wicked, because the blame is meant to be mild and loving.
normal.cn: 家长说 naughty 而很少说 wicked，因为这份责备本意是轻微且带着爱的。

normal.en: A naughty joke is an adult borrowing of the same word: what children should not say, grown-ups giggle at.
normal.cn: naughty joke 是同一个词的成人挪用：孩子不该说的话，大人听了偷笑。

abstract.en: A word that once meant worthless ended up scolding children, showing how harsh words wear soft with daily use.
abstract.cn: 一个曾表示「毫无价值」的词最后用来数落孩子，可见严厉的词在日常使用中会磨得温和。

abstract.en: The crumbs behind the sofa are the whole word: a small wrong that everyone forgives.
abstract.cn: 沙发后面的饼干渣就是这个词的全部：一桩人人都肯原谅的小错。

abstract.en: To call a pleasure naughty is to enjoy the tiny guilt as part of the treat.
abstract.cn: 称一份享受为 naughty，是把那一点点罪恶感当作甜头的佐料。

examples.en: The naughty boy hid behind the door to scare his sister.
examples.cn: 这个调皮的男孩躲在门后吓唬妹妹。

examples.en: Eating dessert before dinner felt very naughty to her.
examples.cn: 在正餐前先吃甜点，她觉得这样真是不够乖。

examples.en: The film had a few naughty jokes but nothing cruel.
examples.cn: 这部电影里有几个下流的笑话，但并不刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹偷」——闹着偷吃饼干的小孩，被大人骂一声 naughty，记住是「调皮的」。

root: 古英语名词 naught（无、恶）+ 形容词词尾 -y 构成，源流清楚；naught 一般重构为日耳曼语的否定复合词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is falling short of good; from it come mild mischief in children and rude humour in adults.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「不及于善」；由此长出孩子的轻微淘气，再滑向成人的下流幽默。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child caught with biscuit crumbs behind the sofa.
core.cn: 核心意象：藏在沙发后偷吃饼干、被逮个正着的小孩。

branches.en: a puppy crouching over a torn cushion while the owner frowns
branches.cn: 小狗咬破垫子，主人在一旁皱眉

branches.en: a child standing in the corner after a scolding
branches.cn: 挨了训斥的孩子面壁站在一角

branches.en: a hand reaching for a second slice of cake at midnight
branches.cn: 半夜里伸手去拿第二块蛋糕

branches.en: friends leaning close and snickering over a whispered joke
branches.cn: 朋友们凑近耳边，为一句悄悄的荤笑话偷笑

branches.en: an adult wagging a finger at a child, then giggling at the same kind of mischief
branches.cn: 大人对孩子摆手指，转头又为同类的顽皮发笑

intro.en: The word family is built on the old noun naught with plain English endings, so every member stays close to the core sense of nothing or no good.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在古名词 naught 之上，配以普通的英语词尾，每个成员都贴近「无、没干好事」的核心义。

latinIntro.en: The word is fully Germanic in origin, and no Latin cognate belongs to this family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全是日耳曼来源，词族里没有拉丁同族词。
